Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Look at a map of the world's cell towers some time. It shocked me.

90% of the Earth has none. Oceans. Deserts. Most farmland.

The technology was never the problem. The cost was.

Then the FCC issued Order DA 24-1193 - giving SpaceX the right to beam a cell signal from space straight to the phone in your pocket. No new phone or installation needed.

Almost overnight, 400 million people came online. And 52,000 more join every day.

But SpaceX only sells the signal. A small firm in Chicago gets paid for what those people do — and it cuts them in. They already have 490 million users across 170 countries. Over $1B earned and saved. And they're the #1 software company according to Deloitte's fastest growing companies list in 2023.

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Look at a map of the world's cell towers some time. Generations of colonists carved a civilization out of the wilderness. They built habits of self-government, forged a prosperous society, and developed the spirit of republicanism that made the American Revolution possible.

In this **FREE documentary-style online course** , you'll learn from Hillsdale professors about the struggles, beliefs, and daily lives that shaped our uniquely American character. The same professors teach our students on campus.

Dear Patriot,
Think about the last time you stood in the grocery store and really felt it. The number at the bottom of the receipt keeps climbing, a cart that used to cost eighty dollars somehow costs a hundred and thirty now, and you quietly put something back on the shelf before you reach the register. You do the math in your head the whole drive home. You work hard and you pay your taxes, and still you have to think twice before you can fill your own refrigerator. **[Now let me show you where some of your money is _actually_ going.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
O'Keefe Media Group released the first part of a new undercover investigation. Our team walked into bodegas and smoke shops in New York City wearing hidden cameras. And one after another, we caught the clerks swiping government EBT cards — **the cards your taxes pay for to help feed hungry families** — to buy kratom, a drug with opioid-like effects. Not food. Drugs. This is your money they are spending, and you can [**help us put a stop to it right now**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). It happened with one clerk after another, all of it captured on camera, in their own words. **"You do what you want with it,"** one of them said about the cash. This program is called SNAP — food stamps — and it costs the country more than $100 billion every year, of which the government admitted that **$10.1 billion went straight out the door in improper payments last year alone.** A USDA investigator says the theft could run as high as $12 billion every year, and that is only the money they are willing to admit to. Sit with that for a moment. At the very moment you are putting groceries back on the shelf, someone else is standing at a counter buying narcotics with a benefits card that you paid for — **your work, your paycheck, your family's money** , handed to people who game the system and contribute nothing in return. Stand with us today and [**help us fund this fight**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). This is the kind of fraud that never gets exposed, because the people gaming it are counting on no one to look. **We looked. And this is only Part 1.** An investigation like this does not stop after a single video, and ours is only just getting started. Our team has to keep going back in, city after city, counter after counter, wearing the cameras and taking the risk, while our lawyers review every frame to make sure it holds up in the open, and none of that comes cheap. Will you [**sponsor this investigation with $25, $50, or whatever you can afford right now**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)? [**Help us follow the fraud all the way to the top**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). You already pay for this fraud-laced program with your taxes, so let's finally make sure you get the truth about where that money actually goes. Thank you for everything you do.
In Truth,James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group
P.S. ****Remember one number the next time you are standing at the register:**twelve billion dollars, gone in a single year** — money that was supposed to feed the millions of families who genuinely need it. We are going to show America exactly who is stealing it, and with your support we will keep the cameras rolling. [**Stand with us**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

Hello Cincinnati!

So much excitement in this room tonight – and I feel the same enthusiasm in Marion and Toledo and Cleveland and Mansfield.

In cities, in suburbs, in small towns, and in farm country, we’ve seen people showing up like never before – Angry. Frustrated. Demanding change.

**They know the system is rigged – more than ever.**

The stock market is up. Corporate profits have soared. Executive salaries have exploded — right now, the average CEO makes $17 million a year. That’s bad enough – what’s worse is that CEOs are making 300 times what their average worker makes.

**Ohio workers are more productive than ever. You work harder than ever.** But no matter how hard you work, your pay is not keeping up and you can’t get ahead.

Families see more money going out the door, and not enough money coming in to pay for utilities, health care, groceries... everything. Big banks pile on fees for every little thing... then they shower their executives with big bonuses.

Insurance companies take your premiums every month – then they do everything they can to refuse to cover the care you need... after they put you on hold for what seems like forever.

Drug companies force you to pay more than people overseas pay for the same drug, the same dosage, and the same packaging, then rake in the profits.

Big corporations gobble up energy to feed their data centers. They devour your land. They suck up your water. They leave you with the bill.

**And no one in Washington is standing up to these corporations who game the system and raise your prices.** Instead, politicians – people who are supposed to work for YOU – are cashing in.

When they’re in office...they play the stock market. When they leave office...they become lobbyists.

**Speaking of...there’s Jon Husted. Special interest Jon in Columbus, now special interest Jon in Washington.

He says struggling Ohioans don’t know how to, quote, navigate the “real world.” **He says you just need to make more money. That you just need to do more work.

And most insulting of all, he says your work ethic is just broken.

Go to Cincinnati Children’s. Talk to a nurse on the night shift... or an orderly pushing a wheel chair... or a worker changing the sheets. Go tell them they need to work harder.

Or go to Frederick Douglas Elementary. Talk to the cafeteria worker preparing food for hundreds of children. Or the school custodian who cleans up after them and cleans the building. Or the teacher who dips into her OWN POCKET to pay for school supplies. Tell them they need to make more money.

**Talk to the workers here at the bar, on their feet all day, and then tell me – no. Tell _them_ – their work ethic is broken.

Everyone in this room – think about your own jobs. How _dare_ Jon Husted say the work ethic is broken. That you aren’t working hard.

Jon Husted, this _is_ the real world. **

It’s bad enough how he talks. It’s even worse what he’s done:

He voted _twelve times_ for the war in Iran that’s raised the price of gas, and groceries, and diesel, and fertilizer. And get this, Husted says the war is going “much better than anyone thought it would.”

Jon Husted voted not once, not twice, but _nine times_ against lowering health insurance premiums. _Nine times._

Why? **He’s taken $700,000 from the same insurance companies that are jacking up premiums in Ohio.**

**He cast the deciding vote to take health care away from 490,000 Ohioans.** Why? All to pay for a tax cut for his billionaire buddies and corporate cronies.

**He was at the center of the largest bribery scandal in Ohio history. A $61 million bribe that hiked up your electricity prices.**

And look at what he’s done with data centers. All 226 of them.

Jon Husted led the charge to bring data centers to Ohio. He delivered giant corporations billions of dollars in sweetheart tax deals. Ohioans now pay thousands more on their utility bills.

It’s exactly what people hate about politics: Special interest Jon Husted works for corporations, not for Ohioans. And we all pay for it. Ohioans don’t have anyone fighting for you.

Until November.

Talk to your neighbors and your friends and tell them: Ohio doesn’t have to accept this corruption. Tell them how we’re going to ban the health insurance companies from denying care that your doctor says you need... if that doesn’t work, we’ll fine them when they deny your claims. Tell them how we’re going to make it illegal for drug companies to charge Americans more than they do in other countries. The same pill should be the same price.

It’s not hard to see why this is happening.

Last year, members of Congress made more than $635 million in stock trades. No wonder they’re not standing up to corporations – they’re too busy lining their own pockets.

No one – _no one_ – who serves in Congress, no spouse, should be able to trade stocks. They also shouldn’t be able to turn around when they leave office and become a lobbyist... **If you can’t agree to that, you shouldn’t be in public office.**

Ohioans won’t stand for this rigged system any longer. Ohio is fighting back.

**You’re showing up. You’re insisting on change.

You’re demanding a senator who will work for Ohio – not for the utility companies, not for the drug companies, not for Wall Street, and not for big oil. Someone who will be on your side.

We’re demanding a government that works for Ohio.

And in 99 days... we’re going to get it.**

Peter,
Last week, the New York Times reported on serious domestic abuse allegations against Congressman Max Miller (R-OH) made by his ex-wife.
Miller scalded his wife's chest and stomach by throwing boiling hot water at her body, held a gun to her head, and slammed her against a wall. He fractured their two-year-old daughter's collarbone and bruised her shoulder.
It was a difficult read, but I refuse to look away: He fractured the collarbone of his two-year-old daughter.

Now we know what he meant: He will not protect women and children. He'll protect his political flock.

I believe women. I stand by domestic abuse survivors, period. My opponent, Mike Johnson, cannot say the same.
My name is Conrad Cable, I'm the Democrat running against Speaker Mike Johnson because I believe that anything less than a full condemnation and demand for Max Miller's resignation is an endorsement of abusers.

This administration, and those who support it, said they were going to drain the swamp. But the swamp is deeper than it ever was.
I sat down with Ali Velshi on MS NOW to discuss the current corruption in Washington DC, the importance of my race in flipping the Senate and the concerns of North Carolina families. You can watch a clip from my interview here:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4cc0faf1-ef6e-489b-9b2e-1b79dbf35f16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a9b1ef7e-5a00-4338-b85a-d8f648c5b533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
_**Ali Velshi:** Joining me now is Roy Cooper, former Governor of North Carolina and Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate. I don't know what to call you, Roy Cooper, because you've been the Governor, you've been the Attorney General. And if I'm recalling correctly, you've not lost an election in the entire time. But you're not taking this one for granted._
_**Gov. Cooper:** No, we can't. There are too many people right now who are telling us that they want political leaders who will focus on the cost of living and the fact that their paychecks just aren't keeping up with it. They're looking at the middle class thinking, "I'll never get there," and they are very frustrated with this administration that promised them that cost of living would be the focus on day one._
_My opponent, Michael Whatley, spent his career as an insider DC lobbyist for Big Oil and utility companies. He owns their stock. The policies he cheers on, like the war in Iran and higher interest rates charged by utility companies, also give him profit. And it 's clear that he's ready to do whatever this administration, whatever this president, wants him to do, regardless of whether it's good for the people of North Carolina._
_This is going to be a close race. It always is in North Carolina. We haven 't elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2008, and in that year, North Carolina voted for Barack Obama for President. It always closes up at the end. There are polls that show things a lot closer than that. I need people's help. I need you to go to [roycooper.com](https://substack.com/redirect/607b54dc-b09a-4dd5-84ac-7fb810d14259?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/e01c04fd-c5a4-485b-9596-a3ce1ab91803?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [help us out,](https://substack.com/redirect/a9b1ef7e-5a00-4338-b85a-d8f648c5b533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [look at our policies](https://substack.com/redirect/c07574b4-d6f5-4914-92ee-df3ae4352cc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to make stuff cost less for North Carolinians. Because this is going to be a tough race, and we have to win North Carolina in order to take back the Senate._
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a9b1ef7e-5a00-4338-b85a-d8f648c5b533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
_**Ali Velshi:** Yeah, very much so. So what can others who are in your position, either trying to hang on to a tenuous seat or win a flippable seat, learn from you? You have managed to win a statewide election in North Carolina when a Republican has won the state in a general election, including Donald Trump. How does that affect how you go out there and campaign? We've seen this in New York, where people will split their vote. They'll vote for you as Governor, someone else as president, someone else as Senator. How do you appeal to that voter?_
_**Gov. Cooper:** Well, I think people want government to work, and they're frustrated right now because the federal government is not working. One of the things that's inspired me on the campaign trail is that there's hardly been an event that I've been to where someone hasn't come up to me and said, "This is the first political event I have ever been to in my life." And it's Democrats, unaffiliated and Republicans who are saying that to me. That shows me that better days are ahead because people are rising up, and I think they're just looking for candidates who will listen to them and who will work hard and do what they think is right._
_This will be by far the toughest race I 've ever been in. I've run for statewide races, and I think people view those differently from federal races. We've seen that in our state. We've seen great candidates be defeated. But the real key here is that we have a candidate in Michael Whatley who will do and say whatever this president tells him to do and say, regardless of whether it's good for the people of North Carolina. And I will be a strong, independent Senator who will focus on the people -- put the people over power, over party, over politics -- and make them my primary focus. I think that's what has gotten me elected in the past, and they've seen me perform. I've got some receipts. I fought Republicans when they needed to be fought, and I've worked with them when I could for good things for North Carolina. That's what they want in a United States Senator as well._
* * *
_**Ali Velshi:** So part of the issue here is Thom Tillis, who's retiring, getting a lot of news these days. Some are painting him as a profile of courage for standing up to Donald Trump, particularly around the issue of Todd Blanche. Well, that didn't last very long, and he still didn't get the deal that he was asking for that guarantees the Trump family isn't isolated from IRS audits for the rest of their lives, which seems like some weird, corrupt deal. This is kind of why we need independent thinkers in Congress, right? We need people to say it is your job as a United States Senator to confirm or deny these appointments, and Tod Blanche didn't cut it._
_**Gov. Cooper:** We all know what this thing is. It's a taxpayer-funded slush fund to pay January 6th rioters and insurrectionists. And you do have a lot of Republicans who are running from it. My opponent, Michael Whatley, openly endorses it, says the pardon of the J6 rioters was okay. Michael Whatley is not only not going to provide oversight for this administration, he's going to be on the Appropriations Committee trying to find a place to make sure they fund the slush fund instead of funding for the people in western North Carolina who are still suffering from Hurricane Helene._
_That 's why it's so important that we take back the Senate majority, because oversight is needed. We need to bring back the checks and balances that the framers of the Constitution intended, on trade and tariffs, on declaration of war, on budgetary matters. It's time for the people to rise up and say enough of this. The legislature is supposed to be a check on the Executive in Washington. That's not happening now. We're seeing it time and again, and we need, as you say, independent thinkers who are going to put party and politics aside and do what's right._
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a9b1ef7e-5a00-4338-b85a-d8f648c5b533?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
_**Ali Velshi:** One of the things - doing what's right. You've got signs behind you that say "Make Stuff Cost Less." You have to go far down the list of members of Congress in the Senate to find somebody who's not worth $50 million. You don't think members of Congress should be able to trade stocks that they have access to inside information on?_
_**Gov. Cooper:** Absolutely not. You know, I think people are yearning for decency. This administration, and those who support it, said they were going to drain the swamp. The swamp is deeper than it ever was. I'm going to be for anti-corruption efforts. We need to overturn Citizens United. We need to get rid of extreme partisan gerrymandering. We've got to make sure that people who are in power don't use their office to enrich themselves, and I'll vote for laws to do that._
_Members of Congress should not buy and sell individual stock. They shouldn 't become lobbyists after they're finished -- nor should high-level people in the executive branch. And I think we need leaders who will do that regardless of whether a law passes because in Washington, they've said they were for it, and they've arranged for them to be able to vote for it in some ways, but then it doesn't pass. So regardless of passing, we need people who are going to stand up and actually do it._
_Before I became Governor, as I was running for Governor, I sold all of my individual stock. I will not buy and sell individual stock as a candidate or as a United States Senator. I won 't become a lobbyist afterward. I'm going to vote for legislation that gets rid of corruption in Washington. It's time for people to stand up and vote for leaders who will do those things, not just say they're going to do them._
_**Ali Velshi:** Governor, good to see you as always. Thank you for joining us._
* * *
As I told Ali, this is going to be a close race. It always is in North Carolina. So I need your help.

But the swamp is deeper than it ever was. I sat down with Ali Velshi on MS NOW to discuss the current corruption in Washington DC, the importance of my race in flipping the Senate and the concerns of North Carolina families. You can watch a clip from my interview here: Ali Velshi: Joining me now is Roy Cooper, former Governor of North Carolina and Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate. I don't know what to call you, Roy Cooper, because you've been the Governor, you've been the Attorney General. And if I'm recalling correctly, you've not lost an election in the entire time. But you're not taking this one for granted. Gov. Cooper: No, we can't. There are too many people right now who are telling us that they want political leaders who will focus on the cost of living and the fact that their paychecks just aren't keeping up with it. They're looking at the middle class thinking, "I'll never get there," and they are very frustrated with this administration that promised them that cost of living would be the focus on day one. My opponent, Michael Whatley, spent his career as an insider DC lobbyist for Big Oil and utility companies. He owns their stock. The policies he cheers on, like the war in Iran and higher interest rates charged by utility companies, also give him profit. And it 's clear that he's ready to do whatever this administration, whatever this president, wants him to do, regardless of whether it's good for the people of North Carolina. This is going to be a close race. It always is in North Carolina. We haven 't elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2008, and in that year, North Carolina voted for Barack Obama for President. It always closes up at the end. There are polls that show things a lot closer than that. I need people's help. I need you to go to , , to make stuff cost less for North Carolinians. Because this is going to be a tough race, and we have to win North Carolina in order to take back the Senate. Ali Velshi: Yeah, very much so. So what can others who are in your position, either trying to hang on to a tenuous seat or win a flippable seat, learn from you? You have managed to win a statewide election in North Carolina when a Republican has won the state in a general election, including Donald Trump. How does that affect how you go out there and campaign? We've seen this in New York, where people will split their vote. They'll vote for you as Governor, someone else as president, someone else as Senator. How do you appeal to that voter? Gov. Cooper: Well, I think people want government to work, and they're frustrated right now because the federal government is not working. One of the things that's inspired me on the campaign trail is that there's hardly been an event that I've been to where someone hasn't come up to me and said, "This is the first political event I have ever been to in my life." And it's Democrats, unaffiliated and Republicans who are saying that to me. That shows me that better days are ahead because people are rising up, and I think they're just looking for candidates who will listen to them and who will work hard and do what they think is right. This will be by far the toughest race I 've ever been in. I've run for statewide races, and I think people view those differently from federal races. We've seen that in our state. We've seen great candidates be defeated. But the real key here is that we have a candidate in Michael Whatley who will do and say whatever this president tells him to do and say, regardless of whether it's good for the people of North Carolina. And I will be a strong, independent Senator who will focus on the people -- put the people over power, over party, over politics -- and make them my primary focus. I think that's what has gotten me elected in the past, and they've seen me perform. I've got some receipts. I fought Republicans when they needed to be fought, and I've worked with them when I could for good things for North Carolina. That's what they want in a United States Senator as well. Ali Velshi: So part of the issue here is Thom Tillis, who's retiring, getting a lot of news these days. Some are painting him as a profile of courage for standing up to Donald Trump, particularly around the issue of Todd Blanche. Well, that didn't last very long, and he still didn't get the deal that he was asking for that guarantees the Trump family isn't isolated from IRS audits for the rest of their lives, which seems like some weird, corrupt deal. This is kind of why we need independent thinkers in Congress, right? We need people to say it is your job as a United States Senator to confirm or deny these appointments, and Tod Blanche didn't cut it. Gov. Cooper: We all know what this thing is. It's a taxpayer-funded slush fund to pay January 6th rioters and insurrectionists. And you do have a lot of Republicans who are running from it. My opponent, Michael Whatley, openly endorses it, says the pardon of the J6 rioters was okay. Michael Whatley is not only not going to provide oversight for this administration, he's going to be on the Appropriations Committee trying to find a place to make sure they fund the slush fund instead of funding for the people in western North Carolina who are still suffering from Hurricane Helene. That 's why it's so important that we take back the Senate majority, because oversight is needed. We need to bring back the checks and balances that the framers of the Constitution intended, on trade and tariffs, on declaration of war, on budgetary matters. It's time for the people to rise up and say enough of this. The legislature is supposed to be a check on the Executive in Washington. That's not happening now. We're seeing it time and again, and we need, as you say, independent thinkers who are going to put party and politics aside and do what's right. Ali Velshi: One of the things - doing what's right. You've got signs behind you that say "Make Stuff Cost Less." You have to go far down the list of members of Congress in the Senate to find somebody who's not worth $50 million. You don't think members of Congress should be able to trade stocks that they have access to inside information on? Gov. Cooper: Absolutely not. You know, I think people are yearning for decency. This administration, and those who support it, said they were going to drain the swamp. The swamp is deeper than it ever was. I'm going to be for anti-corruption efforts. We need to overturn Citizens United. We need to get rid of extreme partisan gerrymandering. We've got to make sure that people who are in power don't use their office to enrich themselves, and I'll vote for laws to do that. Members of Congress should not buy and sell individual stock. They shouldn 't become lobbyists after they're finished -- nor should high-level people in the executive branch. And I think we need leaders who will do that regardless of whether a law passes because in Washington, they've said they were for it, and they've arranged for them to be able to vote for it in some ways, but then it doesn't pass. So regardless of passing, we need people who are going to stand up and actually do it. Before I became Governor, as I was running for Governor, I sold all of my individual stock. I will not buy and sell individual stock as a candidate or as a United States Senator. I won 't become a lobbyist afterward. I'm going to vote for legislation that gets rid of corruption in Washington. It's time for people to stand up and vote for leaders who will do those things, not just say they're going to do them. Ali Velshi: Governor, good to see you as always. Thank you for joining us. * As I told Ali, this is going to be a close race. It always is in North Carolina. So I need your help. Whether you can a few dollars or to knock on doors or call voters, every effort counts. Thank you. P.S. [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, I promise
I’ll keep this short:

I’ve run in a lot of tough races. But this one is unlike any other.

Here in Pennsylvania, we’ve continued to reject the chaos, cruelty, and
corruption coming out of Washington. We’ve shown that government can solve
problems, protect real freedom, lower costs, and get sh*t done.

But if we fall short on Election Day, that backwards brand of politics
could come straight to our Commonwealth’s front door.

Donald Trump’s enablers are already locked in on Pennsylvania. My
far-right opponent would put his agenda ahead of our communities, our
freedoms, and our future.

We can’t give them an inch.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/5457?t=1001&akid=164%2E245147%2EvAh6Ym ]Derek, I know we
can win this race — but only if folks like you step off the sidelines and
get into the game. Will you chip in whatever you can today to help us
reach undecided voters all across Pennsylvania and keep our Commonwealth
moving forward?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

— Josh Shapiro

Peter -Today is a special day in our house—it’s Drew’s birthday! 🎂Campaign life does not leave much time for slowing down, and Drew is usually the last person to make a fuss about himself. But today is his 47th birthday, and I would love your help making sure he feels celebrated.
Drew’s story has always been one of overcoming the odds.
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
He grew up in a trailer in rural Appalachia with a single mother who worked two jobs to make ends meet. Life was not always easy, but Drew never allowed the obstacles in front of him to define what was possible. With the love of his family, the support of his church, and a relentless work ethic, he built a life rooted in perseverance, service, and the belief that hard work can still open doors in America.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | That determination is still at the heart of everything he does today. It is what drives him to fight waste, fraud, and abuse, stand up for taxpayers, and campaign to bring greater transparency and accountability to the Nevada State Treasurer’s Office.
**Here are two ways you can help me celebrate Drew today:**
🎂 **Send him a birthday message.** Leave Drew a note on [Facebook](https://drewfornevada.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d0fe0c7c553b01ff7d246783b&id=2a18cac99a&e=817ed65ac7), [Instagram](https://drewfornevada.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d0fe0c7c553b01ff7d246783b&id=3946869110&e=817ed65ac7), or [X](https://drewfornevada.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d0fe0c7c553b01ff7d246783b&id=01134f46e2&e=817ed65ac7).
🎁 **Chip in $47 for his 47th birthday.** A contribution of $47—or any amount that works for you—will help us reach more Nevada voters and keep building the grassroots campaign we need to win.

I know that hearing from supporters like you will make Drew’s birthday even more meaningful. Thank you for believing in him, standing with our family, and helping us fight for a more accountable state government.
In liberty,Sarah

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: A replica of my skull
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

Friends, can I show you something?
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260805-1-b&t=1&akid=11698%2E3935704%2EJDMWyU)
This is a replica of my skull after being shot in the head. I was at a constituent event when I was the target of a politically motivated shooting. The gunman killed six people and wounded 12 others.
The doctors made a replica of my skull to create the titanium plate that was used to replace the part of my skull that had to be removed due to swelling. I keep it to remind myself of what I survived on that awful day in January 2011.
It’s been fifteen years since my shooting, but not a week goes by when I don’t think about it. Some days are harder than ever, but I never stop fighting.
I see our fight to end gun violence the same way. There have been setbacks, but we can never lose sight of our work to save lives from the gun violence epidemic.
**But too many politicians have shown that they’d rather cave to the gun lobby than fight for our families. As I write this, Donald Trump and his allies are working to roll back our progress and hand massive wins for their gun CEO buddies. Enough is enough.**
Everything is at stake in the midterm elections. I am working to rally voters and elect gun safety champions across the country, but the only way we can continue sharing our message is with your support.
So with less than 100 days until the election, I am personally asking: [**Will you pitch in $10 or more to help GIFFORDS PAC elect leaders in the most competitive of races and power our work to end gun violence?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/65324?c0=giff-em-q32026.dTscjt&refcode=em260805-1-b&t=2&akid=11698%2E3935704%2EJDMWyU)

subject: We did it — now help me FIRE Vindman
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY OLLIVANT FOR CONGRESS
body:
Republicans must unite. Chip in while the iron is hot.

| | | | | [|
---](https://dougforvirginia.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7dcd1f18e4275b5568308150d&id=6398ddfa48&e=14c77a6723)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

**We did it -- you and I.**
Which means I am going to need your help.
For now, we celebrate! I am deeply honored to carry the Republican nomination for the 7th District of Virginia. Your confidence means something to me and Sabrina personally. Republicans now must come together for the real fight that will carry our message of economic prosperity, local affordability, and our shared commonsense conservative values to Washington.
I am a retired Army officer, who seved two combat tours in Iraq, and I live in Culpeper County with my wife, Sabrina. I want more jobs and better jobs, healthier food on our tables, and a secure border.
[**While the iron is hot and the White House is watching, I need you to chip in $500, $100, or even just $25 to keep our momentum strong.**](https://dougforvirginia.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7dcd1f18e4275b5568308150d&id=b12cef2ac6&e=14c77a6723)
Make no mistake: Eugene Vindman is going to have _**millions of dollars**_ in special interest and dark money, and he and his "democratic socialist" friends are going to need _every single penny_ to defend their crazy out-of-touch agenda.
The facts are clear. Under Vindman our groceries bills went up, energy costs skyrocketed, violent criminals roamed our communities, inflation went up, and factories closed. Eugene even tried to fire his own constituents in an illegal referendum in February and hopes Virginians are going to forget about it.
**IN NOVEMBER, you and I are going to send a message back — and** _**FIRE EUGENE VINDMAN.**_
You know what we are up against. I'm ready for the fight, but I need your help TODAY to win.
[**Click here to DONATE $500, $250, $100, $50, or $25.**](https://dougforvirginia.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7dcd1f18e4275b5568308150d&id=d6ce25d83d&e=14c77a6723)
The momentum is on. Can I count on you to help Republicans take back Virginia's 7th District and win in November?

**One Team, One Fight.**
****

**Republican Nominee for U.S. Congress****Virginia’s 7th Congressional District**

name: Alexandra Rojas
subject: BREAKING: Donavan McKinney defeats Shri Thanedar!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

BREAKING, Peter:

Justice Democrat recruit Donavan McKinney just won his primary in
Michigan’s 13th district, beating multimillionaire incumbent Rep. Shri
Thanedar!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260805-1.nH2PBX&refcode=em20260805-38132&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1002&akid=38132%2E1203867%2EQnhdi9 ]Congratulations MI-13 Primary 2026 Winner Donavan McKinney!

For the third time this cycle, a Justice Democrat took on an incumbent and
WON — and that’s thanks to this people-powered, grassroots movement.

In a fight that embodied the fight for the future of the Democratic Party,
a working-class son of Detroit beat a multimillionaire backed by AIPAC and
Crypto’s millions in the bluest, Blackest, and poorest district in the
state.

Donavan beat over $4.5 million in spending, with Shri pouring more than $2
million of his own wealth into the race alongside the Crypto lobby’s $2
million and hundreds of thousands of bundled donations from AIPAC.

Shri first bought his way into Congress in 2022 and quickly sold out to
AIPAC after they sent him on a luxury trip to Israel and endorsed him in
2024. In return, he voted to keep sending weapons and bombs for Israel to
use against the Palestinian people — even when the majority of House
Democrats voted to stop it.

Not only that, but he lied about taking campaign contributions from
corporate super PACs and billionaires. The Crypto lobby and Detroit
utility monopoly DTE both backed Shri, because they knew Donavan couldn’t
be bought.

But Detroiters could see right through Shri and his facade. In yet another
loss to the establishment, voters chose to clean house and send a
progressive champion to represent them in Congress.

Donavan was the first candidate we recruited and the first campaign we
launched in the 2026 cycle — our first primary endorsement in years — and
for good reason. He’s a lifelong Detroiter who’s lived the same struggles
his community faces: growing up, he experienced eviction and homelessness,
has seen his mom work multiple jobs to feed her family, and has the same
asthmatic cough his loved ones have from toxic, polluted air.

He became a union organizer and climate advocate before being elected as a
dedicated state representative for the poorest district in Michigan,
fighting to get corporate money out of politics, workers' rights, and
clean air & water. Now, he’ll bring that same fight to Washington for
Medicare for All, universal childcare, ending military funding to Israel,
holding the corporations raising our prices accountable, and so much more.

Come January, Donavan will be the SEVENTH new Justice Democrat to join our
bloc in Congress and transform the Democratic Party for the better.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260805-1.nH2PBX&refcode=em20260805-38132&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38132%2E1203867%2EQnhdi9 ]We have one more primary fight tomorrow, and then it’s on to the
general election. Will you help us keep winning by chipping in
$5 or more now?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260805-1.nH2PBX&refcode=em20260805-38132&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1022&akid=38132%2E1203867%2EQnhdi9 ]Contribute $5

Thank you again for making this victory possible — we couldn’t have done
it without you.

In solidarity,

Alexandra Rojas
Executive Director

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20260805-38132-footer&t=1023&refcode2=38132_1203867_Qnhdi9&akid=38132%2E1203867%2EQnhdi9

Trump's anti-abortion pick is a vote away from leading the DOJ
**🚨 ACTION ALERT 🚨**
The Senate goes on recess after Friday. [**That means the vote to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general could happen at any moment in the next 48 hours --and your senators need to hear from you before it's too late.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136662253/638193479/-128479760?sourceid=1151519&utm_campaign=27emeus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=blanche&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNjY3N2U1My1kYTkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8wyhNv1U3NVtn1A0e5CXi-zdSUPVobbBnoCWbH8qMz8=&emci=2f677e53-da90-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=36677e53-da90-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

New reporting shows exactly what's at stake. [**In a leaked call, Blanche said the Department of Justice (DOJ) is working with federal health agencies and the White House to make _Dobbs_ permanent in every state.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136662254/638193480/-128479760?sourceid=1151519&utm_campaign=27emeus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=blanche&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNjY3N2U1My1kYTkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8wyhNv1U3NVtn1A0e5CXi-zdSUPVobbBnoCWbH8qMz8=&emci=2f677e53-da90-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=36677e53-da90-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237) He's also pledged to block shipments of medication abortion to ban states and to revisit DOJ guidance on the Comstock Act, putting mifepristone, a drug with a long safety record, squarely in his sights.

**Friend — this is incredible!**
Abdul El-Sayed is officially the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan! I’m proud to have campaigned with Abdul as he put forward his simple message of “Money out of politics, Money in your pocket, Medicare-for-All.” Now we have to do everything we can to make sure Abdul wins the general election:
[**If that’s all you need to hear, rush a split donation between my campaign and Abdul’s so we can keep up the fight in the critical weeks to come >>**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-el-sayed.RYS3tD&refcode=em260805-1-subs&t=3&akid=2413%2E791427%2EbbKAy4)
**[SPLIT A DONATION](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-el-sayed.RYS3tD&refcode=em260805-1-subs&t=4&akid=2413%2E791427%2EbbKAy4)**
Friend, I want to step back and look at the bigger picture:
**We are seeing an unprecedented progressive movement on the rise across this country, and together we are taking power back from MAGA and finally putting the working class first in our politics, not the billionaires.**
Our communities have been through the wringer over the last year and a half. Rising costs. ICE violence. Data centers popping up left and right. Healthcare being ripped away from working families.
Folks are sick and tired of the status quo, and our movement is offering a real alternative; a positive vision of a future you can actually believe in.
So listen, coming off this big victory in Michigan, we have to talk about Minnesota. Our primaries are in just six days, which means we are running out of time to carry this momentum into more wins.
Not only am I running for reelection, but my team is working to turn out voters for Peggy Flanagan for Senate, Keith Ellison for Attorney General, and progressive candidates all the way down the ballot.
**So if you are feeling this incredible energy and want to keep it going, I am humbly, respectfully, asking you to power our efforts to get out the vote by splitting a donation between my campaign and Abdul’s today.**
[**Split $5, $10, or whatever you can afford today and help us get across the finish line in both Michigan and Minnesota. Your donation makes our organizing possible as we fight for the better world we all know is possible. We can’t miss this moment. A year ago, this campaign was a handful of us in a room and a belief: that it shouldn't be this hard, in the richest country in the world, to see a doctor, or pay your bills, or believe your kids will have it better than you did.
We brought this movement to every corner of Michigan, meeting with folks who are sick and tired of the status quo and are ready for change.
Now, it’s time to lock in and keep this must-win Senate seat blue.
But here’s the thing, Derek: **Our Republican opponent Mike Rogers has Trump’s backing, more than $45 million in Super PAC money, and the national GOP on his side.**

I looked at the numbers. Your file is empty. Let's fix that right now. |
Patriot,

I have spent thirty years reading voter data. I know what a healthy file looks like -- and I know what a gap looks like.

Right now, your file has a gap.

**_[The 2026 Republican Policy Assessment is still sitting incomplete — and that is the one thing I need you to fix before tonight.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=5196318e769a4d2694fe55166c2f468f&_e=ZRneZa_U36VEuhXuN5jmkRcNlYoRDY43cSJxPjRdioEfNIE618VX4vwQJ6TBULi3O_TwX4A0EOEVET3hXqDixTG4yp8h9V2DBGSA60ckqciT8By7LizIdjuBbSGBifnQxrk4WDvBagie5K6Gxk-xypPNgL9o_5phlz8wXfEYDNuqTUb0trfXb91zLe1b0QfiHLrPQXLRSQTPK4xq0JBINn0mePWzP62_2oeCNBjgXHY18crJmIYXHC-d8JFm1-QHxSkkpgJ0e-uPEHrJq17mjYkMwhjIZ0vvkf1-4GdxEPyD0kYgtAT_tucHbCR5LS3yOGugruYkNDLAJzyKvSVVcrEwsF6x-um0sLC3ZIoxP1j7hmnAM2QAf0e88zrbujkFSKvMMm_AM2J6wdof5enonZWIOGUfH3xY2KKMfsdKOcNKs7uoeQ3dfT0umCwgMrTF456uHaSvO5o7MWiJyrOtEZ9qWklfEd1qHvBOfNI6OurLDkfH-5yozNIlH_iLUyeoTCgJk3g33081uImyy5Tz6mYdXxvX2H83L_NpBehIyUvHbxwK-MsiLsnrzfxILaQWjlIhovat6gTel8Ga_sdFTVLpVqrUQQL76dGjpPgZKNqkpvoylBkL1mfviRJYkWOsjSEMJEQphoyN0RL4dFw9N6THl-V11qcrBO7PIBKWoShmz2PlbNcIaFkiuxjLJfRdTmQCBkNWXxNDaenAzJfiQfLB9VgVMFB7dSB-EHaJrg4nvlbYnXAgppXXkS-q2u7Q5mCYNBpd18OD4rb0ENJL--uLFxAaUxPqJJbRbwsYnh82bRMNi54Pxlgdt_e3FDH4iBooL6LfJ0uhf5kmE_9K3znyiKo8PN54QAyRM_J3h4mkwIVdPQc01jXEX4vp2XSJqS5Q5Gg_ibUzRgRBxsMh3UBgo8QHk_-eS7jiuUmdr2c%3D)_**

Here's why this matters more than you might think.

When we sit down to build our Senate strategy for November, we go list by list, zip code by zip code. We look at who responded, what they care about, and where the intensity is. That data is how we decide where to fight, where to spend, and where to hold the line.

Democrats are not leaving blank files. Their activists are filling out every survey, returning every call, and showing up at every meeting. They are building the most complete voter intelligence operation this party has ever run -- and they are doing it right now, while most conservatives are still enjoying their summer.

_I have seen elections lost in the data room before the first ad ever runs._

Hey folks,
Michigan just gave us one of the biggest political stories of the year--and it's a lot more complicated than the headlines make it seem.
[Adam Mockler](https://open.substack.com/users/72893096-adam-mockler?utm_source=mentions) and I break down Abdul El-Sayed's razor-thin Democratic Senate primary victory, what it says about the future of the Democratic Party, and why the real challenge starts now. We also talk about the influence of outside money, the fight over the party's direction, and why unity matters more than ever heading into November.
Here are a few moments you won't want to miss:
* **00:01:07** -- Abdul El-Sayed pulls off a stunningly close win, and we unpack what the numbers really tell us about the Democratic coalition.
* **00:03:30** -- Why Democrats need to stop fighting each other and focus on winning the Senate before it's too late.
* **00:06:00** -- We dig into the role of outside money, special interests, and why this race became a test of authenticity.
* **00:10:10** -- Can the progressive and centrist wings actually come together? We debate what the party needs to win in 2028 and beyond.
* **00:13:25** -- The messaging lesson every Democrat should be paying attention to after this election--and why simple, bold ideas still matter.

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26]
Hi Peter,
I’ve been thinking a lot lately about what actually moves people, changes minds, and wins elections.
Social media algorithms are not going to save our democracy. Negative TV ads won't do it either. But talking to our neighbors — really talking, and more importantly, really listening — just might. We can't forget how to do that.
My team and I are out knocking on doors and talking to people across the district. And I have to tell you, it's one of my favorite parts of this job.
I know that might sound like something a politician is just supposed to say, but I really mean it. As an OB-GYN, I spent my career listening to patients, and I bring that same ethic to this work.
I've knocked on thousands of doors over the last few years, and every single time, I'm reminded of why I do this work and fight to make our lives better. The conversations I have with my constituents are always meaningful — whether I’m listening to what they’re worried about, or enjoying the stories they share, or I’m trying my best to answer their questions, even when the answer might be that I don’t know.
It’s these conversations that keep me grounded and motivated to keep going.
It’s also what wins elections. A few years ago, I ran in a tight race for the Minnesota State House, and I ended up flipping a seat that had never been held by a Democrat before by just 216 votes. I really believe knocking on doors made all the difference. All those conversations, all that listening — I'm going to keep doing it, right up through November 3rd, because that’s what really matters here.
But organizing on the ground doesn’t happen on its own. This summer, we’ve built out our ground game with 26 paid interns who are helping us reach as many voters as possible. Supporting those interns, mobilizing our volunteers, printing yard signs — all of it adds up, and all of it is funded by people like you.
So if you've been doomscrolling and wondering what you can actually do right now: this is it. Will you chip in to support our ground game here in Minnesota?

I’ll be sending you daily e-mails from now through the primary election day on Tuesday, so I’ll keep this short.
I’ve been putting together some very clear, very succinct final campaign messages to send out to voters, particularly through social media and on YouTube, headed into Tuesday. I’ve been hearing that there is low turnout so far for early voting in the congressional primaries, and I’m not sure whether that will help me or hurt me. But it does mean there are a lot of people who will be tuning in at the last minute to get a sense of who I am and a brief case for why they should vote for me.
See three videos that I’ve posted and promoted.
The first is built around my go-to one liner: “I think the US Congress is a good idea, and it would be nice if we had one.” I’ve been doing a lot of canvassing and talking to voters on the street, and it’s a sign of the times that whenever I say this, everyone immediately knows what I’m talking about.
Here it is [on Facebook](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=90715bbc67&e=bd44204496), and here it is [on YouTube](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=130f0f8dd8&e=bd44204496). Spread it around.
In the [second video](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=68a5e192e9&e=bd44204496), I compare myself to the other Democratic candidates, emphasizing the fact that I have a "specific, focused message and agenda” that is about the “need to reclaim the power of Congress,” and that “[I’ve got a plan](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=e656847ce8&e=bd44204496)for how to reassert that power.”

Here it is [on Facebook](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=231758f8a5&e=bd44204496), and here it is [on YouTube](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=ba977a9427&e=bd44204496).
Finally, I have [a pitch](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=59088ae2f7&e=bd44204496)aimed partly at Independent voters and disgruntled Republicans who might be considering asking for a Democratic ballot on Tuesday. Virginia is, after all, an open primary state. I warn them that Republicans have built Frankenstein’s monster: an all-powerful presidency which could be used by people they really don’t agree with. “I am running to limit presidential power, to limit this unchecked power, to bring power back to Congress. And I’m willing to limit even the power of a future Democratic president. I’m willing to do that because that way we can limit Donald Trump's power now—and we can also limit the power of whoever comes after him. We can think forward and realize that no one person should have this much power.”

Here it is [on Facebook](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=f46a3e4cf2&e=bd44204496), and here it is [on YouTube](https://tracinskiforcongress.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a57dc258897935e37567f8e43&id=2f33ecd6cd&e=bd44204496).
Again, spread these far and wide. When canvassing yesterday, I encountered some people who had already voted—and many others who were at most vaguely aware that there was a primary coming up. People need the reminder of when and where it is, and who’s running.
Also, if you like what I’m saying, support my campaign. This is your **last chance** to help out before the primary this Tuesday, so please donate **now**.

The week in Mississippi, from The Mississippi Wire. https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/8y8q31ak3a?e=5703353baa

NEWS [Operation Muddy Waters Nets 69 Arrests in Statewide Child Exploitation Crackdown](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=f6afa813ca&e=5703353baa) A two-week operation led by Attorney General Lynn Fitch with federal and local law enforcement produced 69 arrests across Mississippi, officials announced Monday, including 13 on child exploitation charges and 48 sex offender registry absconders. [Continue reading →](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=000c78500b&e=5703353baa) [Former Hinds County District Attorney Jody Owens Permanently Disbarred; Sentencing Set for October 15](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=513a0de0f8&e=5703353baa) The Mississippi Supreme Court has permanently disbarred Jody Owens, who resigned as Hinds County District Attorney after pleading guilty to a federal bribery conspiracy charge. He faces up to five years in prison.[Read →](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=1b2d89376a&e=5703353baa) [Public Safety Department Consolidates Divisions Under New Law, Names Three Senior Officials](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=d92dc590b3&e=5703353baa) Commissioner Sean Tindell has appointed two deputy commissioners and a homeland security director as the Department of Public Safety restructures under House Bill 1612, which consolidates offices within the agency.[Read →](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=68c946ed91&e=5703353baa) [About 170 Foster Students Denied FAITH Scholarships After State Aid Program Runs Short of Money](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=e3f7474340&e=5703353baa) Mississippi's Office of Student Financial Aid told roughly 170 current and former foster youth they would receive no FAITH Scholarship for 2026-27, weeks before the fall semester, after the program was funded below its request.[Read →](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=e42fac2952&e=5703353baa) [Redistricting Hearings Set for Eight Mississippi Towns, Beginning in Tupelo on August 18](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=c3f4841d5d&e=5703353baa) The Legislature's joint redistricting committee has elected its officers, hired outside counsel and scheduled eight public hearings across the state, the first at Itawamba Community College on August 18.[Read →](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=4af397c3c0&e=5703353baa) | Local News
---
[ Leflore Supervisors approve $2 Mn Loan - Settlement amount kept from minutes GREENWOOD -- ](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=12f2461064&e=5703353baa)[ Overtime freeze bid fails - Natchez NATCHEZ -- Motion to freeze overtime payments failed 2 - 3 in cash strapped city](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=f6a8aac484&e=5703353baa)[ Action over nuisance properties STARKVILLE -- Starkville Alderman call for action](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=5e0d1af3e6&e=5703353baa)[ Board approves FEMA bridging loan GREENWOOD -- ](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=243b84b189&e=5703353baa)[ Raise our millage appropriation, asks Community College boss GREENWOOD -- ](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=68076c2c73&e=5703353baa)[ Jackson Council Rejects Budget Amendment at Its Last July Meeting, Days Before State-Law Deadline JACKSON -- The Jackson City Council voted 3-4 on July 29 against amending the fiscal 2025-2026 budget, rejecting the argument of Councilman Kevin Parkinson that state law requires the city to cut appropriations to match revenue collections running well below the $135 million budgeted.](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=4472ed48ac&e=5703353baa)[ Jackson Council Hands Planetarium to Museum of Art in $250,000 Deal, With No Budget Line Identified JACKSON -- The Jackson City Council voted 5-1 to let the Mississippi Museum of Art operate the city’s planetarium under a three-year renewable agreement costing $250,000 at signing and $130,000 a year thereafter — money city officials told the council had not yet been assigned to a budget line.](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=71ce360de0&e=5703353baa)

Today we're thriving.](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=78a0495b2b&e=5703353baa)$79 billion invested since 2020. xAI, Amazon and Aluminum Dynamics chose Mississippi over anywhere on earth. clean_body: The political shockwave is continuing in Michigan. Our three WFP champions for Congress just won a clean sweep! | | | Peter, The political shockwave is continuing in Michigan and the WFP just swept the state! Abdul El-Sayed, Will Lawrence, and Donavan McKinney have campaigned tirelessly across the state, fighting for the working class and fighting against corporate greed. They have weathered record-shattering levels of spending from billionaires and AIPAC, including constant attacks from both the Democratic and Republican establishments. But just like in Pennsylvania, California, New York, New Jersey, Colorado, and DC, those desperate attacks were not enough to slow us down. And now the Working Families Party is poised to send even MORE incredible fighters to Congress. We want to take a moment to talk in-depth about each of these candidates, but first, Let’s talk a bit about these three campaigns, Peter. No Senate candidate in HISTORY has faced more outside spending in a Democratic primary than Abdul El-Sayed. 1 Yet he has remained laser-focused on the needs of working-class Michiganders all year long. We saw the impact first-hand: as WFP organizers worked with partners around the state, it was clear that Abdul’s campaign was energizing countless young voters and those who had previously lost faith in the political system. Those voters have a new political home. WFP was also one of the earliest endorsers of Will Lawrence’s campaign for Congress, at a time when all the national media refused to even mention his name. Like all of our candidates, Will refuses to take corporate PAC money, and he has harnessed the anger and frustration around AI data centers in his district. His long history fighting for climate justice and housing justice was also critical to his campaign. And as a long time member of the WFP, Will’s campaign has been instrumental in building the Michigan WFP. Donavan McKinney stepped up to run against AND BEAT multi-millionaire Democrat Shri Thanedar in the heart of Detroit. Thanedar has been one of the biggest allies of the crypto industry in Congress, and those same crypto PACs spent millions to protect him.1 They failed. And now, Donavan is continuing the string of WFP upsets of Democratic incumbents, including Brad Lander and Melat Kiros. None of these wins happened by mistake. Voters everywhere are beyond sick and tired of status-quo politics. They don’t want leaders who report to AI and crypto lobbies, or AIPAC. They want leaders who will challenge the political establishment, not carry water for it. Thank you for all you’ve done this election cycle, Peter. MS NOW: ‘The largest investment ever’: DNC launches voter registration drive [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080526_1&amount=30]
The 2025 elections showed us a valuable truth, folks: Voter participation is increasing in all the right ways.
Voter registration activity increased across the country. According to the team at National Voter Registration Day, New York recorded more registrations for their 2025 events than in 2024, and California saw similar increases. Earlier this fall it looked like voter participation was going to make a real jump, even in a so-called "off-year".
Then Election Day came. New Jersey had more voters turn out for a gubernatorial election than they had in 20 years. Crucial counties in Pennsylvania saw their highest turnout levels in almost 15 years. New York City reached a turnout percentage unseen in over five decades.
We can drive even higher levels of participation when voters understand the stakes and feel like their vote matters , just like it did last November. That's why our voter registration efforts are so important, and why we work on it all year long.
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. Will you step up with $30 or more today to help register 10 new voters? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=080526_1&amount=30]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

The key is getting young people -- a major target of opponents of voting rights across the country -- to see the importance of voting now more than ever. Pundits in Virginia said they could have called the election results when they saw the first turnout numbers from the major college campus locations around the state. That's the kind of impact these young voters can have.
Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed the last few years.
The upcoming midterm election will determine whether our democracy stays mired in the darkness and conspiracy theories we hear every day or if we can reclaim our rights -- from voting to choice and more -- and march forward to a better future.
New voter registration -- at a cost to us of just about $3 per new voter -- can be game-changing. Abdul al-Sayed, Chuck Schumer, and Haley Stevens
Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Democratic Senate primary this morning, **48.5% to 47.5%, with 99% of the vote counted.** Mallory McMorrow, who dropped out weeks ago, **still pulled 4%.** It was close, but El-Sayed beat Haley Stevens, Chuck Schumer's preferred candidate. Call it El-Sayed's win if you want, but its implications are bigger than that. It is a real blow to Schumer's waning power as Senate Minority Leader.
[AdImpact clocked $98.2 million](https://substack.com/redirect/50cdfc52-07e6-44a7-af9f-4537da687522?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in ads and reserved air through the end of July, the third most expensive Senate primary in American history. Most of it was aimed at one man. It was money lost.
Schumer was already the least popular leader his party has. His approval sits at [28% approve to 47% disapprove](https://substack.com/redirect/fdc4654d-3022-40a6-acf9-4046b505c119?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the worst net rating of any leader in Congress. Michigan is what that weakness looks like spent out in the open. A leader this unpopular, who loses this expensively with this much of the party's money, has run out of the one thing leadership requires. He should step down.
## Democrats Tried to Control This Outcome

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: What just happened in Michigan
body:
It's time to lock in and keep this must-win Senate seat blue.
#
Friends, we did it. We won last night’s primary election.
By the time of the election, the opposition — led by dark money groups and AIPAC — poured more than $70 million on ads for our opponent or attacking us.
We didn't outspend them. We couldn't have.
**We won because hundreds of thousands of you decided this seat wasn't for sale** — not to corporate PACs, not to billionaires, not to anybody writing a check to keep things exactly the way they are.
Grassroots money is the _only_ thing that beats that kind of spending. **It's the only thing that beats it again in November.**
I got into this race because it shouldn't be this hard, in the richest country in the world, to see a doctor or pay your bills or believe your kids will have it better than you did.
Yesterday, Michigan told the political class we're _not_ interested in more of the same broken status quo.
Today, we move into the general election phase of this race with one mission: **Defeat a MAGA Republican who has Trump's blessing and the national GOP's money behind him.**
This victory was well-earned. But now, it's time to lock in and keep this must-win Senate seat blue.
**[If you’re with me, will you add your name today and join me as we continue the fight?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22960?t=1&akid=1701%2E2118727%2EJ69uLG)**
**[Add Your Name ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22960?t=2&akid=1701%2E2118727%2EJ69uLG)**
In solidarity,
Abdul

Newsletter from Rep. Ryan Chamberlin

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/repryanchamberlin/newsletter-from-rep-ryan-chamberlin-kqs1grv7ud-12935116?e=d1c1b9864f)

| | | | |
---
| |
### NEWSLETTER FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN
---
| | Friends and Neighbors,

For the Primary Election, **Early Voting** will begin this Saturday, August 8! It’s hard to believe it’s almost that time again. This weekend, you can visit one of the many **Early Voting locations in Marion County**. Don’t forget to bring your photo ID. In Florida, we take election integrity seriously. Get more information at the [website](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=a2dd439d33&e=d1c1b9864f) of our **Supervisor of Elections, Wesley Wilcox**.
[**https://www.votemarion.gov/317/Vote-Early**](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=e4605d0a56&e=d1c1b9864f)

(And remember, you can also cast your ballot by mail!)
Please let us know if you would like a yard sign or to help us campaign. I always enjoy this time on the campaign trail, meeting with the voters and hearing what you are most concerned about.
As always, please do not hesitate to [**contact my office**](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=2409d17ffe&e=d1c1b9864f) if there is something we can do for you. My team and I would be more than happy to help you in any way we can.

---
| |
### Florida Concrete & Products Association
---
|
---
|
---
| | I enjoyed a tour of a **Florida Concrete & Products Association** cement mill in Sumter County. **Ash Grove Cement** really opened my eyes to the work being done to support Florida’s infrastructure and economic growth. The industry faces many challenges, but I’m proud of what they’re doing to create local jobs in the manufacturing sector, despite the competition from overseas markets. We need more of these kinds of businesses within commuting distance for our local workforce. I’m glad we have pro-America leaders at our state and federal levels who recognize the fundamental value of making things here. Let’s continue to support and expand our manufacturing capacity in this country!

---
| |
### Community Foundation of Ocala/Marion
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
| | I had the opportunity to speak alongside **Jessica McClain** to a packed house full of nonprofit leaders in the **Marion County** area. This is the second year we have held “Your Road to Appropriations,” an educational event put on by the **Community Foundation of Ocala/Marion**. Through these sessions, we have been able to help our nonprofits better understand the process of finding state funding to help with projects that better our community. I look forward to continuing this workshop in future years and hopefully expanding it for other counties to benefit as well.

---
| |
### 10th Annual SKY Valor Award Ceremony & Reception
---
[|
---](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=72a12821cb&e=d1c1b9864f)
[|
---](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=0deea2e29f&e=d1c1b9864f)
| | I attended a very moving and inspiring event, **97.3 THE SKY’s 10th Annual SKY Valor Award Ceremony and Reception**. We heard so many stories of bravery and valor from our first responders. It was humbling to be reminded how much this group serves our county and district, often without our knowledge or recognition. The members of **Marion County Fire Rescue** who were honored had performed heroic resuscitation on an unresponsive three-year old who was feared dead by drowning. Through their immediate action and professional abilities, they were able to save the child and restore him to full health.
It was an honor simply to be present for the ceremony and to show support for those who received the award. Guest speaker **Senator Stan McClain** did an excellent job, and I’m already looking forward to next year’s ceremony.

---
| |
### Endorsements
---
| | I am proud to have earned the endorsements of the **Florida Policy Benevolent Association** and the **Florida Professional Firefighters**. It goes without saying how indebted we are to the men and women of law enforcement and first response who keep us safe and make our communities stronger. In particular, I salute the officers of the **Ocala Police Department** , the deputies of the **Marion County Sheriff’s Office** , and the firefighters of **Marion County Fire Rescue**. I will always work with their leadership to make sure they have the resources they need and full support from those of us in the Florida Legislature.

---
|
---
|
---
| |
### Ending Property Taxes
---
| | As always, let me know what you think about property tax reform in Florida. I continue to campaign for**full elimination of property taxes in the Sunshine State**! I believe we are making progress each day as we build awareness and explain the inexcusable consequences of property taxes for property owners.
Please [follow me on Facebook](https://ryanchamberlin.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ec15c6093052c02efbd22b6cd&id=96475ea4c6&e=d1c1b9864f) to stay up to date. And as always, if you have any questions, don’t hesitate to contact my office.
---
|
---
|
---
| | Thank you for your feedback and for being interested in our state government. These are important issues affecting everyone, and I need **your** help to make progress for our constituents. I look forward to sharing with you again soon.
Best regards,
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **Ryan Chamberlin****State Representative****District 24**

### And the Duke fight continues
| | [Jeff Jackson](https://substack.com/@jeffjacksonnc)
