| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1145021&post_id=209834362&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5ODM0MzYyLCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc4NTk0NTI1OCwiZXhwIjoxNzg4NTM3MjU4LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMTE0NTAyMSIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.tVGE6QHNR5jmybHMcLolQWzzYAm7NbKoWFPHhUrTsHU&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

---
| | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/jeffjacksonnc/p/bad-tow-trucks-in-trouble?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5ODM0MzYyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU5NDUyNTgsImV4cCI6MTc4ODUzNzI1OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTExNDUwMjEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.-jk01-t_UDSzq8x05XkivvVm4PBRM0-8-Gd9hqfgNu8&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

The big news is our Duke Energy case.
In short:
Duke asked to raise your bill by 18%.
We pushed back.
Then they asked to raise it by 11%.
We pushed back.
Now they're asking to raise it by 9.5%.
_Still too high._ We're not agreeing to that, and we're pushing the Utilities Commission - who makes the ultimate decision - for a lower rate.
Why?
Because we ran our own independent analysis of what Duke actually needs to meet growing demand, and we think they overshot. And since you'd be the ones paying the difference, that's a major problem.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c17b3442-6eaa-4294-b322-13b9741532e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There's a second part to this case, and it's about data centers.
Basically:
When a data center (or another large energy user) shows up, it needs new transmission lines and new generation to serve it. That costs a lot, and right now you pay for it - the money comes out of one big pot.
We're trying to keep those costs from shifting to you, and the good news - _maybe_ \- is that Duke has told us they're open to putting those protections in place. The bad news is there's a lot of disagreement on the details, and on something like this the details are everything.
So we're still working on that.
I've got two more Duke Energy cases going on, but I'll save those updates for next time.
### Bad tow trucks in trouble
Sometimes I have to work on something for a while before I can tell you about it. This case was one of those. Here's the story.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9e619ab7-e87e-4ceb-a08b-f0e02b2bc751?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"A1 Towing" operates in Charlotte.
Our evidence showed:
* They towed vehicles they had no authorization to tow.
* They charged more than $4,000 to give a vehicle back.
* They put a second boot on vehicles that were already booted, so they could collect the release fee twice.
* And they were racially targeting the people they towed.

I'm not putting up with any of that, and now we've got a court order against them.
There are about a dozen things they now have to do differently, and all of them are mandatory.
But the main one is money. They have to pay back tens of thousands of dollars to the people they mistreated.
And if they don't pay, they'll owe an additional $100,000. We added that part to motivate them.
My thanks to our civil rights unit for handling this case. Good outcome for victims, and good message to send to predatory towing companies across the state.
### Lighthouse Fund
People are always surprised by this, but it's true.
As things stand, millions of North Carolinians aren't going to hear from me again until the next election.
_Why?_
Because newspapers and local TV just don't reach as many folks as they used to.
That's not ideal. I'd love to share with them the fights we're taking on, like this [video](https://substack.com/redirect/a1ad2895-9b3b-4408-8863-573d19d97c08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on our Duke Energy work:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a1ad2895-9b3b-4408-8863-573d19d97c08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But we can't run TV ads this early. Can't afford it.
However, we _can_ run a monthly digital message (on YouTube, Instagram, etc.) to roughly half a million people in NC.
That costs about $9,500.
So we started the Lighthouse Fund.
Once a month, we deliver a clear beacon to a large group of independent voters in the form of a targeted digital message. This is my way of tapping them on the shoulder and politely saying, "Hi - we're working hard for you, check this out."
It's been a few months since I asked for your help with this, so I'm asking today.
The most effective way to support this is a small, monthly donation - but of course, we'd also appreciate a one-time contribution. You can do either one **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/73af6735-8bcb-49a1-8ca0-581905b857af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (ActBlue) or **[here](https://substack.com/redirect/ab6568e0-4ee1-4454-9fcd-be11e015292e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (non-ActBlue).
Thanks for standing with me.
Best,
Jeff

clean_body: And the Duke fight continues | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more And the Duke fight continues | | | Aug 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | The big news is our Duke Energy case. In short: Duke asked to raise your bill by 18%. We pushed back. Then they asked to raise it by 11%. We pushed back. Now they're asking to raise it by 9.5%. Still too high. We're not agreeing to that, and we're pushing the Utilities Commission - who makes the ultimate decision - for a lower rate. Why? Because we ran our own independent analysis of what Duke actually needs to meet growing demand, and we think they overshot. And since you'd be the ones paying the difference, that's a major problem. | | ---|---|--- There's a second part to this case, and it's about data centers. Basically: When a data center (or another large energy user) shows up, it needs new transmission lines and new generation to serve it. That costs a lot, and right now you pay for it - the money comes out of one big pot. We're trying to keep those costs from shifting to you, and the good news - maybe \- is that Duke has told us they're open to putting those protections in place. The bad news is there's a lot of disagreement on the details, and on something like this the details are everything. So we're still working on that. I've got two more Duke Energy cases going on, but I'll save those updates for next time. Bad tow trucks in trouble Sometimes I have to work on something for a while before I can tell you about it. This case was one of those. Here's the story. | | ---|---|--- "A1 Towing" operates in Charlotte. Our evidence showed: They towed vehicles they had no authorization to tow. They charged more than $4,000 to give a vehicle back. They put a second boot on vehicles that were already booted, so they could collect the release fee twice. And they were racially targeting the people they towed. I'm not putting up with any of that, and now we've got a court order against them. There are about a dozen things they now have to do differently, and all of them are mandatory. But the main one is money. They have to pay back tens of thousands of dollars to the people they mistreated. And if they don't pay, they'll owe an additional $100,000. We added that part to motivate them. My thanks to our civil rights unit for handling this case. Good outcome for victims, and good message to send to predatory towing companies across the state. Lighthouse Fund People are always surprised by this, but it's true. As things stand, millions of North Carolinians aren't going to hear from me again until the next election. Why? Because newspapers and local TV just don't reach as many folks as they used to. That's not ideal. I'd love to share with them the fights we're taking on, like this on our Duke Energy work: | | ---|---|--- But we can't run TV ads this early. Can't afford it. However, we can run a monthly digital message (on YouTube, Instagram, etc.) to roughly half a million people in NC. That costs about $9,500. So we started the Lighthouse Fund. Once a month, we deliver a clear beacon to a large group of independent voters in the form of a targeted digital message. This is my way of tapping them on the shoulder and politely saying, "Hi - we're working hard for you, check this out." It's been a few months since I asked for your help with this, so I'm asking today. The most effective way to support this is a small, monthly donation - but of course, we'd also appreciate a one-time contribution. You can do either one (ActBlue) or (non-ActBlue). Thanks for standing with me. Best, Jeff ? P.S. - Every year, NCDOJ goes to a Durham Bulls game as a office event. body:
This win is OURS
| | | | Hi Friend,
As I sit here the morning after voters across VA-10 chose me as their nominee for Congress, I can't help but be filled with overwhelming gratitude.
But this win isn't mine alone. **It belongs to every single one of you, too.**
Every volunteer who knocked on doors sharing my message, every donor who believed in this campaign before anyone knew my name, and every family who welcomed us onto their porch this summer to talk about what matters to them. _Thank you for trusting me with this fight._
_Now the real work begins._
VA-10 deserves a representative who will fight for fiscal responsibility, keep our communities safe, stand behind law enforcement, and defend our constitutional rights. That's the choice voters will have this November, and I won't take a single vote for granted between now and then.
But to accomplish this, **Republicans across VA-10 need to come together** to strengthen our party, welcome every voter who wants real change, and stay focused on one goal: **defeating Suhas Subramanyam this November**. That kind of win doesn't come from the top down, it comes from neighbors helping neighbors, one conversation, one door, one phone call at a time.
_If you're ready to be part of that, here's how you can help_ :
\- Sign up to volunteer for door knocking days, to make calls, or to help at events \- Chip in with a donation, no amount is too small \- Share this campaign with a friend or family member who you think needs to hear my message
---
| | | [DONATE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
---
| [VOLUNTEER](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
---
| | |
---
Every single person who joins this effort makes us stronger heading into November. I'm energized, excited, and I know **WE can defeat Suhas** this fall.
Thank you, from the bottom of my heart, for standing with me thus far. Let's keep going, together, to restore faith in the American Dream.
God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_
|
---

Pete Hegseth needs to get a grip.
The Defense Secretary recently announced his plan to test our service members for testosterone levels, making hormone therapy available for older men deemed to have “low t.”
This is from the same party that is determined to criminalize reproductive and gender affirming care.
As a critical care physician, I can say with confidence that this is utter nonsense.
Hormone levels depend on a variety of individual factors. What is low for one person may be completely normal for another. Worse, unnecessary testosterone injections can have serious consequences for patients, including sterility.
It’s yet another attempt by Hegseth, who has never served in a senior military role nor attended medical school , to try to force a bizarre right-wing interpretation of manliness.
As someone who had the honor of treating our nation’s finest for many years, I will not stand by while Hegseth disrespects them in the name of his fragile masculinity.
He’s dangerous, he’s unfit, and he’s unethical. He cares more about fighting Trump’s culture war than supporting real soldiers.
We need him and his boss out of the White House. If you agree with me, help us reinstate guardrails for our democracy by flipping the House and Senate this November >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_med_email-26q3?refcode=x_260805_testosteronetesting_act]

body:
Wes Moore Loses the Triple Crown. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/e8cddfbea341/preakness-disaster-6756185?e=5bb5efcda7)
---
| |
---
| |
# Wes Moore's UnJustified, Unmitigated Preakness Disaster.
**Dear friend,** I was there with four of my children when Justified crossed the finish line and won the Triple Crown. Maryland's Preakness had been the second historic leg of that victory, like it had since at least 1919.

[](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=44fc819c05&e=5bb5efcda7)

But now Wes Moore appears to have gambled away Maryalnd's prestige, our history, heritage and horse racing.

Wes Moore promised that his administration’s **$85 million purchase of the Preakness rights** would secure Maryland’s place at the center of American horse racing. This was a disastrous use of our taxpayer money.

Immediately after his "deal" was finalized, Churchill Downs and the New York Racing Association announced a new national championship series that [excludes the Preakness](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=40f586f0f5&e=5bb5efcda7), isolating Maryland and placing the historic Triple Crown tradition in grave jeopardy.

Maryland’s place in the Triple Crown, through the Preakness Stakes, historically generated approximately $41 million in annual economic activity, including nearly $12 million in tourism spending, $15 million in wages, and almost $3 million in state and local tax revenue. It has a **$2 billion estimated direct economic impact of Maryland’s entire equine industry**.

Moore’s reckless gamble has become an **unjustified, unmitigated disaster** for Maryland and for one of America’s most treasured sporting institutions.

For generations, the Preakness brought national prestige, tourism and economic opportunity, and unforgettable family memories to Maryland. Yet under Wes Moore, taxpayers and racing revenues are being committed to enormous debt while Maryland’s signature race is pushed toward the sidelines. Leadership is not measured by expensive press releases or government ownership, it is measured by results. Moore promised to protect the Preakness, but his failed leadership has endangered the very tradition he claimed he was saving.

**Join our campaign and[donate today](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=ac2f4a1381&e=5bb5efcda7).** We need to raise the money to beat Wes Moore and any amount helps, whether [$25, $50, $75, $100, $250 (for America's 250th Anniversary!), $1000, $2500 (Maryland's 400!), $3000, $6000](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=45e1529cef&e=5bb5efcda7) (max per person and per business).

Together, we will restore responsible leadership, rebuild Maryland’s national prestige, protect the Preakness, and return our state to its glorious days of tradition, toursim, prosperity, and wholesome family fun. Maryland deserves a governor who will defend our heritage, not spend millions presiding over its decline.

For Maryland,
[](https://dancoxforgovernor.us13.list-manage.com/track/click?u=866897dcd900340c866a1068a&id=4707138ad4&e=5bb5efcda7)
Dan Cox, Nominee for Governor

subject: Six days to go. Let’s finish strong.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Berge for Congress_
body:
Find a canvass launch or volunteer opportunity and help Team Berge reach more voters before the primary.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| | | | | |
# This Week with Team Berge
---
| |
Hi Team Berge,
We are officially less than one week away from the August 11 primary!
Every conversation, door knocked, phone call made, event attended, and post shared has helped us reach this point. Now, we have less than a week to make sure voters across the district know who Emily is, what she stands for, and why their vote matters.
This final week is our chance to turn all of the momentum we have built into votes. Whether you have been with us from the beginning or are looking for a way to get involved for the first time, there is still time to make a meaningful difference.

---
| |
# Join us on Election Night!
---
|
---
| |
Come celebrate the work this team has accomplished and watch the results come in with Emily, campaign volunteers, supporters, friends, and neighbors. We hope to see you there!
---
| |
# Get Your Network to Vote!
---
| |
One of the most helpful things you can do before Election Day is remind your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers to make a plan to vote for Emily.
Please reach out to the people in your network and encourage them to vote on Tuesday, August 11. Voters can find their polling place, view a sample ballot, and get personalized voting information at [**www.myvote.wi.gov**](https://confluencewi.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=19cee66bc82e58a6987393ac7&id=912c0578e2&e=1362dd258a).
Every vote and conversation matters!
---
| |
# Help Us Finish Strong
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
Every community event is an opportunity to listen, connect, and introduce more voters to Emily. Join Team Berge at one of the upcoming events below and help us continue building this campaign from the ground up.
**Wednesday, August 5**(5:00pm-7:00pm) - Viroqua Meet and Greet**Thursday, August 6**(4:00pm-6:00pm) - Texting for Berge Happy Hour (Point Brewery in Stevens Point)**Sunday, August 9**(9:30am-1:00pm) - Potosi Catfish Festival Parade

**Sunday, August 9**(6:00pm-8:00pm) - Text for Emily Party (1929 3rd Street, Eau Claire)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | [Sign Up to Volunteer](https://confluencewi.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=19cee66bc82e58a6987393ac7&id=0345e1a31b&e=1362dd258a)
---
| |
# Help Us Reach Voters
---
| |

The most important thing we can do during this final week is connect directly with voters. We have several canvassing and volunteer opportunities available, and every shift helps us reach more people before Election Day.
You do not need any previous experience to participate. Our team will provide everything you need, and you will be joined by other volunteers who are working toward the same goal. Even an hour of your time can help us knock more doors, make more calls, and remind more voters to make their voices heard. Let’s make these final days count!
**Saturday, August 8**(10:00am-11:00am) - Knock doors in Eau Claire (Launches from 440 Broadway Street)**Saturday, August 8**(10:00am-2:00pm) - Local Leaders Canvass Launch and Rally in La Crosse (Launches from 2220 Division St)**Saturday, August 8**(11:00am-1:00pm) - Knock doors in La Crosse (Launches from 332 Front Street S.)**Sunday, August 9**(12:00pm-2:00pm) - Knock doors in Tomah (Launches from 1216 Mark Avenue)
Want to canvass closer to home or help in another way? Complete our [Canvassing Form](https://confluencewi.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=19cee66bc82e58a6987393ac7&id=b76a6d620e&e=1362dd258a), and a member of Team Berge will help you find the right opportunity.
---
| [Join a Canvass Launch](https://confluencewi.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=19cee66bc82e58a6987393ac7&id=53ec6c9efd&e=1362dd258a)
---
| |
# Support the Campaign from Anywhere
---
| |

Can’t attend an event this week? There are still several easy ways to help increase Emily’s visibility and reach more voters:
Request a Berge yard sign:[ Yard Sign Request Form](https://confluencewi.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=19cee66bc82e58a6987393ac7&id=2014483d96&e=1362dd258a)Submit a written testimonial about why you are supporting Emily:[ Submit a Story](https://confluencewi.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=19cee66bc82e58a6987393ac7&id=912b4302db&e=1362dd258a)Boost social media engagement by liking, commenting on, and sharing campaign posts. Follow Berge for Congress on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, and Bluesky.Wear your Berge button around town. Volunteers have shared great stories about conversations started with neighbors, cashiers, servers, and community members just by wearing a button.**Have a question about an event or how to get involved? Just reply to this email and we will help get you connected!**
---
| |
# Thank you for being a part of Team Berge!
---
| |
Thank you for everything you have done to support Emily and this campaign. Your time, energy, encouragement, and belief in what we are building have brought us this far.
This campaign is powered by people who care deeply about their communities and believe that western Wisconsin deserves strong, thoughtful representation. We are so grateful to have you on this team.
Let’s finish strong and make the most of every day we have left. We can do this together!

Peter, now, you're probably wondering why there's a photo of me with Santa in your inbox in August. We definitely missed Christmas in July. _But, I have a confession to make about this picture._

Looking at it now, it's pretty obvious that the young man with the red mustache next to me was not Old St. Nick. But the little girl in this photo? **She was absolutely, completely, 100% convinced she was meeting the real Santa Claus.**

When I was little, I thought Christmas just... happened. Only years later did I understand how much work my parents put into giving my siblings and me that feeling of wonder. They found pockets in the budget when there really wasn't room. They stayed up late after we had gone to bed. **They carried the stress so we could enjoy the magic.**

I realized that's not something parents do only at Christmas. **They make those little miracles happen all year long.** In the summer, they're setting money aside to make sure their kids have everything they need for a new school year. In the fall, they're somehow pulling together the perfect Halloween costume. All this happens while juggling busy work schedules, the bills, healthcare costs, and so much more — it's hard work!

But I know I'm not speaking for just myself when I say it's all worth it to protect our children's sense of possibility and help them believe in the extraordinary.

**Our families deserve leaders who work just as hard for them.** That's one of the reasons I'm running for Congress. The choices representatives make in Washington either make it easier or harder for families to build the lives they want. My goal is to make choices that help every parent spend less time worrying about making ends meet, and more time creating those moments their kids will remember for the rest of their lives.

body:
Government spending should never be a black box. Help me open the books.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/f117d7556e3f/protecting-your-dollars-10146498?e=8837fbc313)

Marylander,

**You deserve to know exactly how your money is being spent.** For too long, state finances have _**operated with limited visibility**_. Taxpayers are asked to trust that billions are managed wisely:**without clear, real-time access to the numbers**. That lack of transparency _**erodes public trust**_ and _**makes waste, fraud, and abuse**_ harder to catch.**I am running for Comptroller to change that.**
---

Building a campaign that prioritizes **openness** and **accountability** requires resources.**Help me bring full transparency to Maryland government by making a contribution today!**

That lack of transparency erodes public trust and makes waste, fraud, and abuse harder to catch.I am running for Comptroller to change that. | | As your Independent Taxpayer Watchdog, I will deliver full transparency by:✅ Building near real-time financial dashboards so every Marylander can see revenues, spending, and audit results✅ Publishing clear, accessible reports instead of buried documents✅ Treating taxpayer dollars with the same accountability responsible families demand in their own householdsTransparency is the foundation of trust and fiscal responsibility. The general election is November 3. Building a campaign that prioritizes openness and accountability requires resources.Help me bring full transparency to Maryland government by making a contribution today! | | | Maryland taxpayers deserve leadership that opens the books and puts people first. Join me in this fight for accountability.Thank you for standing with me. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Let’s Get It DUNN,Sonya Dunn Republican Nominee for Maryland ComptrollerMaryland’s Money. The chairman of the Special Olympics, who is also RFK’s cousin, joined thousands of disability advocates and called on the administration to PROTECT the disabled community – which is their legal responsibility. **This outcry is because of a memo from the Justice Department that argues that states do not have to provide in-home or community-based care to people with disabilities.****** The disabled community deserves to work and live with their family and friends without the fear of being forced into an institution that does not have the resources to make their lives fulfilled. **Without the federal government requiring that states help disabled people integrate into their communities, this has the momentum to create a second-class citizenship for disabled Americans.****** We could see states plunging disabled folks into darkness to keep them out of sight. clean_body: | Friend, Tomorrow,Thursday, August 6th , is primary election day. We are down to the final hours of this campaign, and everything we have poured our hearts into comes down to this moment. When I launched this campaign, people asked why an underdog, a public defender, and a mom would take on the political establishment. The answer is simple : because Tennessee families deserve better than just scraping by — they deserve stability, dignity, and a government that actually fights for them. We're fighting for what matters to you: Fully funded public schools and respected teachers, while standing firmly against private voucher schemes that drain our classrooms. Working families first ,** fighting for paid family leave, affordable childcare, a true living wage, and immediate economic relief. Healthcare as a fundamental right , expanding Medicaid across rural Tennessee and protecting reproductive freedom. Common-sense gun safety, including universal background checks, red flag laws, and safe storage because no parent should ever have to fear sending their child to school. **Wednesday, August 5, 2026 -**_** ** Iran's talks with Oman about the Strait of Hormuz in final stages, have "nothing to do" with the U.S. Qatari Foreign Minister: Multinational effort underway to reach diplomatic resolution to Iran War. Report: Iran demands say over inbound and outbound Hormuz traffic. Iraq in Hormuz talks with Iran, Iraqi official says. At least 56 executed in Iran since March, UN human rights chief says. Israeli abuse of Palestinian "doctor of the poor." Israeli Knesset committee approves around 110 million dollars for settlement expansion. Israel orders evacuation, launches strikes after explosion kills soldiers in south Lebanon. Primary results from Michigan, Missouri, and Kansas. ICE arrests hit record 51,000 in July. Trump administration refunds $100 billion in "liberation day" tariffs. Appeals court rules Environmental Protection Agency cannot block $20 billion in climate grants. Rep. Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after Ethics Committee recommends censure for sexual harassment. Democrat Julian Beaudion withdraws from South Dakota Senate race. AP: Trump administration has detained more than 50 relatives of active-duty troops in immigration crackdown. Russian barrage on Kyiv kills at least 17. Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return to Bangladesh despite death sentence. U.S. revokes visa of Brazilian ambassador. Brazil downgrades diplomatic ties with Argentina after President Javier Milei's latest insults of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Mass jail break, armed clashes kill three in cities west of Tripoli. Malaysia says it won't repatriate Rohingya refugees to Myanmar if their lives are at risk. Ceuta seeks transfer of 1,100 unaccompanied minor migrants to mainland Spain._
**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.ed8RqIIgEafd52-Tvbjl_rzc5SosS0TqywJ0cURgTLc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=209945600)
* * *
# Iran
* **Tehran 's Hormuz talks with Oman in final stages, have "nothing to do" with U.S.: **Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Wednesday that Iran and Oman have agreed on the geographic parameters of a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz and are in the final stage of preparing a joint announcement, provided "certain third parties" do not interfere.
* An agreement on shipping arrangements between Iran and Oman through the Strait of Hormuz would not immediately reopen the waterway, a government source [told](https://substack.com/redirect/98670913-5922-4320-9804-c1e240c9edf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, saying that the ongoing talks have "nothing to do" with the U.S. The source told the broadcaster that the waterway would remain closed as long as "U.S. violations" continue.
* Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained severely restricted on Tuesday, with just eight vessels transiting the waterway for a second consecutive day, according to shipping data firm Kpler. Prior to the war, roughly 130-140 ships typically passed through each day.
* **Qatar FM: Multinational effort underway to reach diplomatic resolution to Iran War:** Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al-Ansari [said](https://substack.com/redirect/2a7b2e61-01ba-4af6-9e1e-e48b21071076?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday Doha is coordinating with Oman, Pakistan, and GCC states to broker a U.S.-Iran diplomatic resolution and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
* He called mediation efforts "ongoing" and said a draft of a possible agreement was being circulated among the relevant parties, adding that the talks have reached "very progressive stages."

* **Report: Iran demands say over inbound and outbound Hormuz traffic:** Iran is demanding control over ships [entering](https://substack.com/redirect/93e1f639-b6db-4e8c-b486-239e19222bf1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Strait of Hormuz and oversight of outbound traffic, with the power to intervene if necessary, under a temporary reopening plan being discussed with Oman, a senior Iranian source told Reuters on Tuesday.
* Outbound vessels would travel between Iran and Oman, with Oman granting exit clearance after notifying Tehran, Reuters reports.
* The source told the outlet that Iran has already compromised from its initial demand for full control in both directions and is unlikely to shift further.

* **Iraq in Hormuz talks with Iran, Iraqi official says:** Iraqi Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f9c2d796-e066-427e-b65a-71ccde142329?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday that the country is in talks with Iran over the "smooth flow of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz," expressing hope for a breakthrough in the coming days, according to a statement carried by the Iraqi News Agency.
* Iraq exports roughly 95% of its crude through the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, leaving the major OPEC producer heavily exposed to the disruption caused by the waterway's effective closure.
* The talks come days after Iraq signed a separate agreement with Turkey to maintain northern crude exports to the Mediterranean through the Ceyhan pipeline, bypassing the Gulf.

* **At least 56 executed in Iran since March, UN human rights chief says:** Iran has executed at least 56 people on national security-related charges since March 19, including 27 in cases linked to mass anti-government protests in January, according to United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk, with over 100 others at risk of execution on similar charges. "I am alarmed by the rise in executions and death sentences issued in Iran since March, and that capital punishment continues to be used to instill fear among the population and suppress dissent," Turk said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/947ed486-04ec-4229-9ad9-5aff132e34ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He added that executions for drug-related offenses are also continuing "at an alarming rate."

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah claims attack on Saudi tanker:** Yemen's Ansarallah movement announced on Tuesday that it had struck the Saudi oil tanker Wafa with ballistic missiles in the northern Red Sea, off Yanbu, claiming a direct hit as part of enforcing its maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia, though neither the Saudis nor major maritime tracking firms confirmed the incident.
* Ansarallah said its forces have now targeted eight Saudi oil tankers since the blockade began on July 22, adding that 29 Saudi tankers have been prevented from continuing their voyages and forced to turn back in the Red and Arabian Seas.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed after succumbing to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and one was injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Two bodies were also recovered from beneath the rubble.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,381 killed, with 174,231 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,254 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,121, while 804 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israel 's assault on Gaza:**
* Israel struck and [wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/8e84cefc-7a55-4086-8cd0-292f8e391dd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian child on Wednesday morning, west of Khan Younis, according to Shehab News.
* Israeli artillery [shelled](https://substack.com/redirect/7ed6e6f7-0851-4c92-8847-d86c3ea182d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an area northeast of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza on Wednesday, WAFA reported, and also fired on the northern areas of Al-Bureij refugee camp.
* In the southern Gaza Strip, Israel shelled areas southwest of Khan Younis.
* **Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank:**

Photo by Finn Gomez/Getty Images. Wednesday, August 5, 2026 - Iran's talks with Oman about the Strait of Hormuz in final stages, have "nothing to do" with the U.S. Qatari Foreign Minister: Multinational effort underway to reach diplomatic resolution to Iran War. Report: Iran demands say over inbound and outbound Hormuz traffic. Iraq in Hormuz talks with Iran, Iraqi official says. At least 56 executed in Iran since March, UN human rights chief says. Ansarallah claims attack on Saudi tanker. Israel's assault on Gaza continues. Israel carries on with attacks in the occupied West Bank. Israeli military probe says soldier may have killed settler in Tal attack. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he has "disagreements" with President Donald Trump over the Gaza plan. Israeli abuse of Palestinian "doctor of the poor." Israeli Knesset committee approves around 110 million dollars for settlement expansion. Israel orders evacuation, launches strikes after explosion kills soldiers in south Lebanon. Primary results from Michigan, Missouri, and Kansas. ICE arrests hit record 51,000 in July. Trump administration refunds $100 billion in "liberation day" tariffs. Appeals court rules Environmental Protection Agency cannot block $20 billion in climate grants. Rep. Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after Ethics Committee recommends censure for sexual harassment. Democrat Julian Beaudion withdraws from South Dakota Senate race. AP: Trump administration has detained more than 50 relatives of active-duty troops in immigration crackdown. Russian barrage on Kyiv kills at least 17. Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return to Bangladesh despite death sentence. U.S. revokes visa of Brazilian ambassador. Brazil downgrades diplomatic ties with Argentina after President Javier Milei's latest insults of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Mass jail break, armed clashes kill three in cities west of Tripoli. Malaysia says it won't repatriate Rohingya refugees to Myanmar if their lives are at risk. Ceuta seeks transfer of 1,100 unaccompanied minor migrants to mainland Spain. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Tehran 's Hormuz talks with Oman in final stages, have "nothing to do" with U.S.: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Wednesday that Iran and Oman have agreed on the geographic parameters of a shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz and are in the final stage of preparing a joint announcement, provided "certain third parties" do not interfere. An agreement on shipping arrangements between Iran and Oman through the Strait of Hormuz would not immediately reopen the waterway, a government source Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, saying that the ongoing talks have "nothing to do" with the U.S. The source told the broadcaster that the waterway would remain closed as long as "U.S. violations" continue. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained severely restricted on Tuesday, with just eight vessels transiting the waterway for a second consecutive day, according to shipping data firm Kpler. Prior to the war, roughly 130-140 ships typically passed through each day. Qatar FM: Multinational effort underway to reach diplomatic resolution to Iran War: Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al-Ansari on Tuesday Doha is coordinating with Oman, Pakistan, and GCC states to broker a U.S.-Iran diplomatic resolution and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He called mediation efforts "ongoing" and said a draft of a possible agreement was being circulated among the relevant parties, adding that the talks have reached "very progressive stages." Report: Iran demands say over inbound and outbound Hormuz traffic: Iran is demanding control over ships the Strait of Hormuz and oversight of outbound traffic, with the power to intervene if necessary, under a temporary reopening plan being discussed with Oman, a senior Iranian source told Reuters on Tuesday. Outbound vessels would travel between Iran and Oman, with Oman granting exit clearance after notifying Tehran, Reuters reports. The source told the outlet that Iran has already compromised from its initial demand for full control in both directions and is unlikely to shift further. Iraq in Hormuz talks with Iran, Iraqi official says: Iraqi Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair on Tuesday that the country is in talks with Iran over the "smooth flow of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz," expressing hope for a breakthrough in the coming days, according to a statement carried by the Iraqi News Agency. Iraq exports roughly 95% of its crude through the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, leaving the major OPEC producer heavily exposed to the disruption caused by the waterway's effective closure. The talks come days after Iraq signed a separate agreement with Turkey to maintain northern crude exports to the Mediterranean through the Ceyhan pipeline, bypassing the Gulf. At least 56 executed in Iran since March, UN human rights chief says: Iran has executed at least 56 people on national security-related charges since March 19, including 27 in cases linked to mass anti-government protests in January, according to United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk, with over 100 others at risk of execution on similar charges. "I am alarmed by the rise in executions and death sentences issued in Iran since March, and that capital punishment continues to be used to instill fear among the population and suppress dissent," Turk said in a . He added that executions for drug-related offenses are also continuing "at an alarming rate." Yemen Ansarallah claims attack on Saudi tanker: Yemen's Ansarallah movement announced on Tuesday that it had struck the Saudi oil tanker Wafa with ballistic missiles in the northern Red Sea, off Yanbu, claiming a direct hit as part of enforcing its maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia, though neither the Saudis nor major maritime tracking firms confirmed the incident. Ansarallah said its forces have now targeted eight Saudi oil tankers since the blockade began on July 22, adding that 29 Saudi tankers have been prevented from continuing their voyages and forced to turn back in the Red and Arabian Seas. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed after succumbing to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and one was injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Two bodies were also recovered from beneath the rubble. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,381 killed, with 174,231 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,254 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,121, while 804 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel 's assault on Gaza: Israel struck and a Palestinian child on Wednesday morning, west of Khan Younis, according to Shehab News. Israeli artillery an area northeast of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza on Wednesday, WAFA reported, and also fired on the northern areas of Al-Bureij refugee camp. In the southern Gaza Strip, Israel shelled areas southwest of Khan Younis. Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank: East Jerusalem: A large force of Israeli soldiers Qalandia refugee camp, north of Jerusalem, on Wednesday morning, conducting searches and raids, and detaining several Palestinians. Israeli soldiers distributed leaflets stating that "a large-scale operation" in the camp was underway, according to Quds News Network. The Palestinian Red Crescent said its crews in the camp have so far treated eight people who were assaulted. The army operation comes one week after Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued instructions to occupy another Palestinian refugee camp under the model of the army invasions of the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in early 2025 that Human Rights Watch said amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity. In a separate attack in the town of Al-Ram, Israeli soldiers a young Palestinian man in the foot, according to the Red Crescent. Bethlehem: Israeli forces the town of Beit Fajjar on Tuesday evening, firing tear gas and sound bombs. In Nahalin, west of Bethlehem, Israeli settlers demolitions on three Palestinian homes. Jenin: Israeli forces four Palestinians in several raids on the Jenin governorate on Wednesday, seizing one home in the area and converting it into a military barracks. Settlers Palestinian land and uprooted olive trees in nearby Ajja, receiving support from the Israeli military, according to WAFA. Tubas: Israeli settlers a water pipeline in Yerza, East of Tubas, on Wednesday, according to WAFA, the eighth attack on this pipeline since the beginning of July. Galilee: Israeli forces a Palestinian home in Al-Ba'na in Galilee on Wednesday, forcing evacuations from the area, and detaining the home's owner and his brother when they attempted to resist the operation. Israeli military probe says soldier may have killed settler in Tal attack: An Israeli military investigation published Wednesday that friendly fire may have killed Israeli settler Benayahu Mellet during a deadly settler attack in the occupied West Bank village of Tal last month, The Times of Israel reported. Four Palestinians and two Israelis were killed during the attack after around 20 settlers, some of them armed, stormed the village. The incident sparked a large-scale Israeli military operation across the occupied West Bank. According to the probe, Mellet died shortly after a Palestinian wrestled a rifle from another Israeli, though the military said it could not determine whether he was killed by Palestinian fire or by Israeli troops because his body was buried without an autopsy. Netanyahu says he has "disagreements" with Trump over the Gaza plan: After meeting with "Board of Peace" representative Nickolay Mladenov on Tuesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Israeli media that he had "disagreements with President Trump" concerning "the recent agreement with Hamas." Netanyahu maintained, contrary to the roadmap published by the board, that Hamas "must be disarmed and the Gaza Strip [be] demilitarized before moving to the reconstruction phase." During the meeting, Mladenov reportedly urged Netanyahu to halt Israeli attacks on Gaza, two sources told the AP. Following the meeting, Hamas from the board, the AFP reported, voicing "unease" over Mladenov's statement after he met with Netanyahu. The statement, a Hamas official said, "focused solely on the issue of weapons and failed to address the occupation's obligations," which include an end to all Israeli attacks on Gaza. Israeli abuse of Palestinian "doctor of the poor": Israeli prison guards have a 71-year-old Palestinian doctor, tear-gassed his overcrowded cell, and denied him vital medication, according to testimony published by Haaretz on Tuesday. Dr. Mazen Al-Rantisi, nicknamed the "doctor of the poor" because of the free and low-charge medical care he provides Ramallah-area residents, was imprisoned by Israeli forces during a raid on June 21, and was indicted for chairing a health nonprofit previously outlawed by Israel. Al-Rantisi told a lawyer from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel this week that guards force blindfolded prisoners to walk bent over, beat him and other detainees during repeated raids, and fired tear gas into their cells. Younger prisoners surround him during the beatings in an effort to shield him. Israel withheld all of his regular prescriptions for his first 10 days at Ofer Prison and continues to deny him one medication. His requests to see a doctor have been ignored, and his lawyer said he has lost significant weight. Drop Site video dispatch from mass funeral in Gaza: 44 children and 37 women were among 112 members of the Al-Hasayna and Abu Sharia families laid to rest at a mass funeral in northern Gaza after Civil Defense crews recently recovered their bodies from beneath the rubble. Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah shared footage from the funeral and spoke with attendees. "The first house was bombed, so they fled to a second house, then to a third, searching for somewhere safe to hide," family elder Nahed Al-Hasayna told Drop Site. "These were all children and women, peaceful and innocent. For what crime were they killed?" Fares Affana, director of ambulance and emergency services for Civil Defense in northern Gaza, told Drop Site that Israeli attacks had systematically destroyed Gaza's rescue capacity, leaving crews unable to reach people trapped beneath collapsed buildings. "We could hear the cries and screams of the wounded from beneath the rubble....But because we lacked equipment, we could not reach them," he said, adding that many remained trapped for days until they died. Watch Sabbah 's full report . Israeli Knesset committee approves around 110 million dollars for settlement expansion: The Israeli Knesset Finance Committee a special session Tuesday during the election recess to approve 335 million shekels (~$110 million) for settlement expansion, which would raise the Israeli Settlement Ministry's budget for the year to a record 821 million shekels (not including the 944 million shekels it has committed for future settlements). Lebanon Israel orders evacuation, launches strikes after explosion kills soldiers in south Lebanon : Israel launched a wave of attacks across southern Lebanon on Wednesday after two Israeli soldiers were reportedly killed and others wounded after an explosive device detonated inside a building in Majdal Zoun, a village in southern Lebanon that is partially occupied by the Israeli military, according to Israeli media. Following the explosion, the Israeli military claimed Hezbollah had violated the ceasefire and ordered residents of Al-Mansouri to evacuate north before two airstrikes on the Mashaa al-Mansouri area south of Tyre (Sour). Israeli artillery also shelled the outskirts of Majdal Zoun, according to Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA). An Israeli airstrike the rooftop of a prayer room at the Tebnine cemetery, killing one person and wounding 11 others, according to NNA. Israeli forces also illumination flares over the heights of Kfar Reman, which NNA said were intended to ignite fires, while troops to forested areas and fruit orchards in Houla, with the flames spreading to homes in the town's western neighborhoods. Israel has continued carrying out near-daily attacks in Lebanon despite the U.S.-brokered ceasefire. On Tuesday night, Israeli forces carried out another large-scale demolition in Hadatha in Bint Jbeil district and a drone struck the same location twice in the Roueiss neighborhood of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, according to NNA. U.S. News Primary results: Abdul El-Sayed beat Rep. Haley Stevens in Tuesday's Michigan Democratic Senate primary, overcoming over $60 million in outside funding, mostly from pro-Israel groups, and late endorsements of Stevens from current Gov. Gretchen Whitmer and prominent national Democrats like Rep. James Clyburn. El-Sayed will face Republican Mike Rogers in the November general election. If elected, he will be the first Muslim-American to serve in the U.S. Senate. State Rep. Donavan McKinney prevailed over incumbent Democratic Rep. Shri Thanedar in their Detroit-area primary contest, despite Thanedar's backing from AIPAC and cryptocurrency interests. McKinney, a 34-year-old endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America, is now the heavy favorite to represent the safely Democratic district. Progressive William Lawrence two moderate candidates in his Democratic primary in the Lansing Area. Lawrence, a climate organizer endorsed by** Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rashida Tlaib , will face incumbent Republican Rep. Tom Barrett , rated one of the most vulnerable Republican incumbents in this cycle, in the general election to represent Michigan's 7th district in the House. Rep. Wesley Bell defeated former Rep. Cori Bush in Missouri's 1st Congressional District Democratic primary, repeating his 2024 win over Bush, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America. AIPAC spent about $3 million on Bell's behalf, less than the $8 million he received in 2024, when he was one of the largest beneficiaries of AIPAC spending nationwide. Missouri voters a Republican-backed measure that would have required a majority in each of the state's eight congressional districts, rather than a simple statewide majority, to pass citizen-sponsored constitutional amendments, preserving a tool voters have used to pass measures including Medicaid expansion, marijuana legalization, and an abortion rights guarantee. Opponents, including a state real estate association and abortion rights groups, noted the measure would have set the highest such threshold among the 18 states allowing citizen-led constitutional amendments and that none of the four amendments Missouri voters passed since 2020 won in all eight districts. Rev. Adam Hamilton , pastor of the largest United Methodist congregation in the country, won Tuesday's Democratic Senate primary in Kansas, according to The Associated Press, setting up a challenge against Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in a state that hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate in nearly 100 years. Though Kansas has not factored into Democrats' plans to retake the Senate, Hamilton is viewed by some as a talented fundraiser and has some political tailwinds, including the recent re-election of a Democratic governor and an electoral victory for abortion rights in 2022. Kansas voters a Republican-backed ballot measure that would have required state Supreme Court justices to be popularly elected rather than appointed by the governor, dealing another setback to lawmakers seeking to overturn a 2019 court ruling that established a constitutional right to abortion in the state. Kansas Republicans had campaigned for the measure by arguing that the state Supreme Court had failed to represent the "will" of the state's voters, but told anti-abortion groups that the referendum was aimed at challenging the state's abortion laws. Abbas Alawieh won his Democratic primary to represent the Dearborn area in the state Senate. Before his work on behalf of the "Uncommitted" movement, which attempted to hold the Democratic Party accountable for its failures on Gaza. Alawieh previously served as a congressional aide to Reps. Andy Levin , Rashida Tlaib, andCori Bush. If elected, he will be the first Arab-American to serve in Michigan's state Senate. ICE arrests hit record 51,000 in July: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement 51,000 people in July, the largest single-month total in Department of Homeland Security history, according to sources familiar with the data cited by ABC News. ICE has particularly ramped up its campaign at American airports, with 30 people detained at airports in July, according to the data. Trump administration refunds $100 billion in "liberation day" tariffs: The Trump administration has about $100 billion, or 60% of the $165 billion collected, in refunds of "liberation day" tariffs since the Supreme Court struck down the emergency powers used to impose them earlier this year, according to a report U.S. customs officials gave judges at the U.S. Court of International Trade on Tuesday. Customs and Border Protection said in a Tuesday court filing that more than $128 billion has been "accepted for processing," indicating that more refunds are imminent. Representative Greg Casar(D-Texas) noted that the refunds go almost exclusively to companies, and are not seen by consumers. "Every single cent of these refunds should go back to American consumers," he said on X. Appeals court rules E.P.A. cannot block $20 billion in climate grants : A divided 10-judge panel on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit an injunction Tuesday barring the Environmental Protection Agency from terminating $20 billion in climate grants under the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund, ruling that recipients should have access to the funds while their case proceeds. If the E.P.A. does not appeal to the Supreme Court within seven days, the ruling will effectively reinstate the Biden-era program, which E.P.A. Administrator Lee Zeldin sought to kill, using as his pretext unsubstantiated allegations of waste and fraud against eight climate groups. Rep. Chuck Edwards drops re-election bid after Ethics Committee recommends censure for sexual harassment : Rep. Chuck Edwards , a North Carolina Republican, from his re-election campaign early Wednesday after the House Ethics Committee recommended censure after finding he sexually harassed two female staffers and created a hostile work environment. The House is expected to vote on censuring Edwards after the August recess. Edwards said in a post on X that he would complete his current term. Democrat Julian Beaudion withdraws from South Dakota Senate race: Julian Beaudion , the Democratic nominee for South Dakota's Senate seat, from the race Tuesday after months of vowing to stay in, clearing the way for a one-on-one contest between independent Brian Bengs and Republican incumbent Mike Rounds , The Washington Post reported. South Dakota becomes the third state where Democrats have opted not to field a Senate candidate, following Nebraska and Idaho, a strategy that gained traction after independent Dan Osborn came within seven percentage points of winning Nebraska's 2024 race. Beaudion said he would not endorse either Bengs or Rounds and accused Bengs, without naming him, of "intimidating threats to drop out of this race." AP: Trump administration has detained more than 50 relatives of active-duty troops in immigration crackdown : More than 50 parents and spouses of active-duty U.S. service members have been under President Donald Trump's second-term immigration crackdown, with at least six deported, according to an Associated Press investigation published on Wednesday. The detentions, which experts say reverse decades of bipartisan practice protecting military families and even Trump's own first-term policy, have disrupted deployments and left troops without childcare, including Army Sgt. Hedar Leonel Turcios Juarez , whose wife was detained outside a Walmart, and Air Force Tech. Sgt. Wendy Gbeve , whose father was deported to Mexico despite a pending legal status application. DHS said in a statement that "military service alone does not automatically grant lawful immigration status," even as Army and National Guard recruiters continue advertising immigration benefits like "military parole-in-place" to potential enlistees. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Russian barrage on Kyiv kills at least 17: Russia Kyiv and surrounding areas with 24 ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles, and 115 drones early Wednesday, killing at least 17 people, according to Al Jazeera, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying the strikes hit warehouses, a brewery, and construction supply sites. Zelenskyy said Ukraine's supply of air defense missiles is three times lower than in 2025 and that missile interceptors "could have saved the lives of those killed today." Reuters that U.S. officials are discussing options to replenish Ukraine's depleted Patriot stockpiles, including allowing domestic component manufacturing. Separately, Ukraine struck a Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tula region and an oil refinery in Bashkortostan on Wednesday. Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return to Bangladesh despite death sentence: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, 78, in a video address on Wednesday that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December after two years in exile in India, despite a death sentence handed down against her. Hasina, who was ousted following a violent crackdown on protests in 2024, made the announcement alongside her son, Sajeeb Wazed Joy, and other leaders from her Awami League Party. She said the exact date of her return would be announced "when time comes." U.S. revokes visa of Brazilian ambassador : The United States the visa of Brazilian Ambassador to Washington Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti. The move comes after Brasilia stalled the approval of the incoming U.S. envoy and refused visas for two U.S. State Department officials over concerns of political meddling. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defended the move by openly accusing the American diplomats of seeking to interfere in the October vote and cast doubt on the integrity of the country's electoral system. State Department officials indicated the ambassador's credentials could be reinstated once Brazil accepts Washington's choice for the post. Brazil downgrades diplomatic ties with Argentina after Milei 's latest insults of Lula: Brazil will relations with Argentina at the charge d'affaires level after Argentine President Javier Milei again insulted Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, calling him an "ex-convict," a "thief," and "corrupt" in recent interview on Argentine television, a Brazilian government source told Reuters on Tuesday. Brazil's ambassador to Argentina, Julio Bitelli, who had already been recalled last month after Milei criticized Lula while campaigning alongside opposition candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, will not return to Buenos Aires. Milei and Lula have not held an official bilateral meeting since Milei took office in December 2023. Mass jail break, armed clashes kill three in cities west of Tripoli : Detainees a mass escape from a jail in Surman, near Tripoli, on Tuesday as armed clashes between rival groups erupted in the nearby cities of Zawiya and Surman, killing three civilians and injuring several others, Reuters reported. The origin and cause of the clashes remained unclear. Zawiya, located 40 kilometers west of Tripoli, is home to Libya's largest functioning oil refinery, which urged workers to avoid the areas of fighting. Surman's Mayor Mohamed Abu Snina described the humanitarian situation as "very bad" but said relative calm had returned to the city after a neutral force was deployed to the area. Malaysia says it won 't repatriate Rohingya refugees to Myanmar if their lives are at risk: Malaysia will not with repatriating 5,000 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar if their lives are found to be at risk, government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil said Wednesday. Fahmi said Myanmar's junta government is ready to receive the refugees but that Malaysia's foreign and home ministries are still reviewing the plan before proceeding. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's government sought the handover after unrest between the Rohingya refugees and Malaysians, in response to which Rohingya schools were shut down, and some refugees were evicted from homes in Penang or briefly detained after gathering outside the UNHCR building in the country's capital. Ceuta seeks transfer of 1,100 unaccompanied minor migrants to mainland Spain: Local leaders in Spain's Ceuta are the transfer of roughly 1,100 unaccompanied minors to mainland Spain after 72,000 migrants arrived in the enclave in one week, Reuters reported on Tuesday. While most migrants have since returned to Morocco, the minors cannot be summarily deported and remain in makeshift accommodations in the city. Ceuta government head Juan Jesus Vivas called the situation "absolutely unsustainable." name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Action
subject: One more push before recess
body:
The Senate should not adjourn until it passes the bill 87 percent of Americans already support.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/0100019fd2c93f66-1fde4a72-22fb-478e-8d4a-3749e828a2c0-000000/VfZKZQMJrTQmKF7q3TJwOnG0c0THqAMKFOnlakCh4tA=452)Patriot–I know you are tired.Your fingers are tired of dialing. You have called, written, and shown up, over and over, telling your members of Congress to pass the SAVE America Act.I am tired too. I am tired of pushing Republican Senators to do the one thing that the overwhelming majority of American voters, including a strong majority of Democrats, already asked them to do.But the Senate is about to leave Washington for the August recess. So I am asking you for one more push before they go.**Here is what I need you to do today:**
1. Call the Capitol switchboard at **202-224-3121** and ask to be connected to your United States Senator. Then call back and ask for your other Senator. Both offices need to hear from you.
2. Tell each office this: **Do not leave Washington for the August recess until the Senate passes the SAVE America Act.**
3. Send the same message in writing at [_**tpp.me/saveamericaact**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Ftpp.me%2Fsaveamericaact/1/0100019fd2c93f66-1fde4a72-22fb-478e-8d4a-3749e828a2c0-000000/vdb_fZE_GpKiSATZCJ3srkwMVdZUld5TTIfQYrRLcWc=452). It takes less than a minute.

[PASS THE SAVE AMERICA ACT](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org%2Fsave-america-act%2F/1/0100019fd2c93f66-1fde4a72-22fb-478e-8d4a-3749e828a2c0-000000/FCd-8H5nkVF4vQMONy04pOZy5lqDjwjdBcXJZ0hElKA=452)This bill is not complicated. It requires documentary proof of United States citizenship in order to register to vote in a federal election, and it requires photo identification when casting a ballot. That is it. Eighty seven percent of Americans support it. Seventy three percent of Democrats support it. The House passed it. The Senate has been sitting on it for more than a year.Senators do not move because the argument is good. They move because the phone lines will not stop ringing and the mail will not stop coming. That is the only reason this bill is still alive, and it is the only thing that will get it to the floor before the Senate goes home.One call today. Both offices. Then forward this to one person who will do the same.The Senate should not go home until the job is done.Fighting for America,Jenny Beth Martin
Chairman
Tea Party Patriots Action**P.S. If the Senate adjourns without acting, this fight sits idle until September and the calendar only gets shorter.** If you do nothing else today, pick up the phone and call **202-224-3121**. Ask for each of your two Senators and tell them to stay in session until the SAVE America Act passes.[CONTRIBUTE](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org%2Fdonate%2F/1/0100019fd2c93f66-1fde4a72-22fb-478e-8d4a-3749e828a2c0-000000/_W6s2zsguQXl8cPiLI81A_Om0bMH8EZNhur3olSXU68=452) _This email list is a joint venture of the following separate organizations: Tea Party Patriots Action, Inc., Tea Party Patriots Foundation, and Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund. By the grace of God we earned a huge 85% win in the primary for Virginia's 5th District last night. The highest percentage of any contested congressional primary in Virginia.

This is the best endorsement of what we are doing in the district to support our constituents and help put more money back in the pockets of hard working Americans!

From 2019 to 2025, Maine spent more than $22 million in state and federal tax dollars on syringe services programs -- that is, "clinics" where intravenous drug users can get needles for free, 100 at a time.
What did we get for all that cash?
The distribution of 17.2 million free needles -- 2.3 million of which remain uncollected -- and the largest HIV/AIDS and hepatitis C outbreak in generations. On top of that, Maine saw drug addiction and drug-related crime soar. Of course, the progressive district attorneys refuse to prosecute criminals, so cops stop making futile arrests, and then the DAs crow that crime is down when the only thing that's actually down is crime fighting. Ask any cop in Maine and he will tell you the same thing: the majority of crime flows directly from narcotics trafficking and narcotics addiction.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc04469f-4f95-4d06-86db-8831cf29986a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In 2023, there were 8,373 drug addicts -- sorry, individuals suffering from substance use disorder -- picking up free needles at the taxpayer-funded clinics. The next year, that number almost doubled to 15,949, according to the state's own reports. If we're measuring the success of the needle program by the number of needles handed out, then it's going smashingly. The trouble is that the program's ostensible purpose was to limit the spread of bloodborne illnesses. By that measure, it's failed beyond even the most cynical predictions.

In case you missed the news, Maine is currently experiencing the worst outbreak of HIV in the state's history. All of it is drug-related, all connected directly to a taxpayer-funded needle giveaway in Penobscot County. Confirmed cases have now risen to 45. The original cluster of 24 cases flagged last year stemmed entirely from intravenous drug users who were patrons of the same NGO syringe program. The [Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)](https://substack.com/redirect/af894357-83a4-482c-9e4d-f77879fdb1bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reports that 91 percent of the currently infected patients injected drugs within the last year. Of the 45 patients, 40 have a hepatitis co-infection -- also the result of fentanyl injections.
In other words: Maine's worst-ever HIV and hepatitis outbreak happened exactly as progressive Democrats dumped millions of dollars into testing the proposition that giving away free needles would limit the spread of diseases like HIV and hepatitis.
It's safe to say the results of the experiment are in. The progressive "harm reduction" policies haven't just failed to reduce harm. They've actually caused more harm. This is a catastrophic failure of the public health policies championed by Gov. Janet Mills, her policy guru Hannah Pingree, and all of the "harm reduction" cultists at DHHS and Maine CDC.
To begin with, Mills [suspended](https://substack.com/redirect/a0d80ba3-c0e8-4a42-a34e-41acda2ea115?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the 1-to-1 needle exchange requirement to save us all from the China Virus. How'd that work out? Can we get an accounting of how many lives were saved because drug users could get 100-packs of syringes without turning in needles, rather than under the long-standing requirement that one needle returned earned you one clean needle? I have a feeling the number of lives saved as a result of this imbecilic policy is about the same as the number of words Mills will utter admitting the abject failure of her policies. That is, zero.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/31440d77-246b-4b02-805c-ca8d66d9dd2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Compounding the unscientific lurch toward harm reduction policies, Democratic lawmakers then permanently loosened the syringe service rules and poured state cash into the NGO complex that shovels needles into the street: Down East AIDS Network / Health Equity Alliance, Maine Access Points, Wabanaki Public Health and Wellness, Church of Safe Injection, Tri-County Mental Health Services, Spurwink, and the rest.

The legislative paper trail is not subtle -- and legislative Republicans have some of the infected blood on their hands, too. The 128th Legislature enacted Public Law 2017, chapter 464 ([LD 1707](https://substack.com/redirect/703b9458-94f2-4c4e-97bb-e274cd1dde72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)), putting $75,000 behind hypodermic exchange programs. That effort required some Republicans to join Democrats in overriding Gov. Paul LePage's veto. (You can see who voted for the "Act To Reduce the Cost of Care Resulting from Blood-borne Infectious Diseases" [here](https://substack.com/redirect/7721dba4-4f16-420d-92fa-34e275c4ae2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).) But that unwise policy move was peanuts compared to the torrent of cash Mills and her Democratic allies would then pour into needle programs.
Post-2018, the Mills administration stacked on roughly $2 million from the Fund for a Healthy Maine to expand needle distribution sites, then $800,000 and later $1 million from the [Opioid Use Disorder Prevention and Treatment Fund](https://substack.com/redirect/46a910b0-9f4b-4101-821d-a1e380b66dd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), then another [$1.92 million for 2023-2025](https://substack.com/redirect/d2deabff-0ca1-4221-a818-c99965318d0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- on top of the original $75,000 annual baseline and late-2024 opioid-settlement awards of $75,000 per site, per year. In 2021, Democrats went further and decriminalized possession of syringes with residual drugs. In 2022, DHHS locked in the [1-to-100 rule](https://substack.com/redirect/1935c254-dfb3-4368-a9d2-db51a88c2fa7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Mills had created by executive fiat: bring nothing, leave with up to 100 free needles. In 2025, with the Bangor-area HIV outbreak already raging, the Legislature passed another law ([LD 1078](https://substack.com/redirect/5ee5046d-196f-4049-80fe-a629789958e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) to expand mobile and rotating exchange sites.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..f3NCXnXGVXF2zjq0wHHIFMWSyQd0nPu8LyeXl0A9LCI?)
Before the policy free-for-all, Maine's exchanges typically collected as many syringes as they handed out -- or more. In the 2019 [reporting year](https://substack.com/redirect/6f222805-7f60-486c-8820-83508937c5c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Maine's syringe service programs distributed about 880,000 syringes and collected about 949,000. Back-calculate from that year's 15 percent jump and you get roughly 764,000 distributed in 2018, with collections again exceeding distributions. In other words, the 1-to-1 policy was giving hard drug users clean needles without littering the streets with infectious hazards. Then Mills and the Legislature blew the doors off. Official Maine CDC reports to the Legislature show the explosion:
* 2020: 1.67 million [distributed](https://substack.com/redirect/41ee5f39-85ce-4de0-a191-cae68000e563?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 1.31 million collected
* 2021: 2.70 million [distributed](https://substack.com/redirect/64731e59-6721-488b-a3e1-44fd290697ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 2.02 million collected
* 2022: 2.37 million [distributed](https://substack.com/redirect/9f3ca100-9f14-4862-aebe-6871eb289caa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 2.43 million collected
* 2023: 3.68 million [distributed](https://substack.com/redirect/46a910b0-9f4b-4101-821d-a1e380b66dd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 3.16 million collected
* 2024: 3.19 million [distributed](https://substack.com/redirect/9d130516-96fe-4c50-90cc-b1d02de962c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 2.49 million collected
* 2025: 2.70 million [distributed](https://substack.com/redirect/51380b9a-ac0f-4c7e-94ca-b7c6fb9f33c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 2.48 million collected

Add it up for the Mills era (2019-2025 reporting years): about **17.2 million** syringes handed out and about **14.8 million** collected. Roughly **2.3 million** never came back. That is a standing inventory of dirty needles in parks, riverwalks, playgrounds, encampments, [Bangor's hidden drug enclaves](https://substack.com/redirect/4de39e85-0a0e-47e2-9f6c-cb4a4c427034?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and storm drains -- paid for by the working families who can no longer let their kids run barefoot.
Sanford's city manager [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/70e05431-19da-40f0-afe5-c2e1dbbbdaa8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) roughly 14,700 used syringes pulled from a single encampment next to a Maine Access Points site. Portland's two programs alone were nearly 300,000 syringes underwater in a single year. In Bangor, Health Equity Alliance -- the dominant taxpayer-backed exchange -- distributed about 659,000 syringes in the 2023 reporting year and about 589,000 in 2024 before collapsing amid financial mismanagement.
The human cost is not theoretical. A three-year-old was stuck by a discarded hypodermic on the Brewer Riverwalk this week -- a [story first reported by The Maine Wire's Joe Sokol](https://substack.com/redirect/02020d8d-9718-4ef6-b66a-9d4ca5cb9603?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and subsequently ripped off shamelessly by the Bangor newspaper. Former Lewiston City Councilor Ryn Soule was [stuck in April](https://substack.com/redirect/29eaf34f-a102-45e6-98e7-fb53cebe0b0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and hospital-treated while the city still debated more "harm reduction" money. Dogs get the same treatment on the same lawns and trails. Every public space becomes a minefield of taxpayer-funded sharps potentially laced with fentanyl residue and blood borne disease. And the one theoretical public good these programs were supposed to supply, i.e. protecting intravenous drug users from spreading HIV, backfired in the worst way imaginable.
The only good thing you can say about Maine's opioid policies is that overdose fatalities have decreased slightly statewide from the record high of 606 deaths in 2023. But that reduction in deaths is attributable to two things. First, the same people funding free needle carts in every city also handed pharmaceutical companies a ton of cash to distribute Narcan, the overdose reversal drug, for free all over the state. The people living in tents on Maine's city streets, when asked what kind of services they get from the city, have told us that a few times a month someone will come by and toss them a few Narcan doses. One of those men admitted to having been "Narcan'd" more than a dozen times over the last year.
The second factor in Maine's slight fatality reduction, probably the largest factor, is that [Dominican drug trafficking organizations like the Trinitarios](https://substack.com/redirect/dcf0f3f3-a07a-441c-9273-116487046c4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) started pushing meth and less potent blends of fentanyl. The Dominican drug traffickers are savvy businessmen, and they realized they were killing their clients too fast. An addict who fatally overdoses within six months is worth less over the long-term than an addict who survives at least a few years. That's the ruthless logic of the international drug trafficking organizations that have been exploiting Maine while liberals talk about "restorative justice" and abolishing the police. Opioid deaths are down, slightly, but fentanyl addiction and the crime that spirals outward from it is raging like wildfire. And the policy designed to mitigate the spread of diseases related to intravenuous drug use, ie needle exchange programs, have incontestably failed.

Hannah Pingree has not had much to say about any of this in public. Last month, Mills went to the epicenter of rising opioid deaths and HIV cases to claim victory at the "[opioid response summit](https://substack.com/redirect/38221e32-a411-4d84-b59a-bcdf2e1a0211?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Pingree's only comment at the summit was that Maine needs to do more, but we're left to wonder whether she means more of the failed policy. She spent six-plus years as Mills' director of the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future -- the shop that co-owned the state's opioid and "innovation" agenda -- before leaving the administration in May 2025. Given that resume, it's reasonable to expect that a Governor Pingree would mean more "harm reduction" -- that is, more needles, more NGO contracts, more mobile vans, and higher costs for the working people who now walk their kids past biohazards in what used to be ordinary public parks. Like most everything undermining the quality of life in Maine, it was a choice. A new class of political leaders could easily make a different choice. They could choose not fund the rot infecting our cities and instead fund effective law enforcement.
