To begin with, Mills the 1-to-1 needle exchange requirement to save us all from the China Virus. How'd that work out? Can we get an accounting of how many lives were saved because drug users could get 100-packs of syringes without turning in needles, rather than under the long-standing requirement that one needle returned earned you one clean needle? I have a feeling the number of lives saved as a result of this imbecilic policy is about the same as the number of words Mills will utter admitting the abject failure of her policies. That is, zero. | | ---|---|--- Compounding the unscientific lurch toward harm reduction policies, Democratic lawmakers then permanently loosened the syringe service rules and poured state cash into the NGO complex that shovels needles into the street: Down East AIDS Network / Health Equity Alliance, Maine Access Points, Wabanaki Public Health and Wellness, Church of Safe Injection, Tri-County Mental Health Services, Spurwink, and the rest. This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. The legislative paper trail is not subtle -- and legislative Republicans have some of the infected blood on their hands, too. The 128th Legislature enacted Public Law 2017, chapter 464 (), putting $75,000 behind hypodermic exchange programs. That effort required some Republicans to join Democrats in overriding Gov. Paul LePage's veto. (You can see who voted for the "Act To Reduce the Cost of Care Resulting from Blood-borne Infectious Diseases" .) But that unwise policy move was peanuts compared to the torrent of cash Mills and her Democratic allies would then pour into needle programs. Post-2018, the Mills administration stacked on roughly $2 million from the Fund for a Healthy Maine to expand needle distribution sites, then $800,000 and later $1 million from the , then another -- on top of the original $75,000 annual baseline and late-2024 opioid-settlement awards of $75,000 per site, per year. In 2021, Democrats went further and decriminalized possession of syringes with residual drugs. In 2022, DHHS locked in the Mills had created by executive fiat: bring nothing, leave with up to 100 free needles. In 2025, with the Bangor-area HIV outbreak already raging, the Legislature passed another law () to expand mobile and rotating exchange sites. ? Before the policy free-for-all, Maine's exchanges typically collected as many syringes as they handed out -- or more. In the 2019 , Maine's syringe service programs distributed about 880,000 syringes and collected about 949,000. Back-calculate from that year's 15 percent jump and you get roughly 764,000 distributed in 2018, with collections again exceeding distributions. In other words, the 1-to-1 policy was giving hard drug users clean needles without littering the streets with infectious hazards. Then Mills and the Legislature blew the doors off. Official Maine CDC reports to the Legislature show the explosion: 2020: 1.67 million , 1.31 million collected 2021: 2.70 million , 2.02 million collected 2022: 2.37 million , 2.43 million collected 2023: 3.68 million , 3.16 million collected 2024: 3.19 million , 2.49 million collected 2025: 2.70 million , 2.48 million collected Add it up for the Mills era (2019-2025 reporting years): about 17.2 million syringes handed out and about 14.8 million collected. Roughly 2.3 million never came back. That is a standing inventory of dirty needles in parks, riverwalks, playgrounds, encampments, , and storm drains -- paid for by the working families who can no longer let their kids run barefoot. Sanford's city manager roughly 14,700 used syringes pulled from a single encampment next to a Maine Access Points site. Portland's two programs alone were nearly 300,000 syringes underwater in a single year. In Bangor, Health Equity Alliance -- the dominant taxpayer-backed exchange -- distributed about 659,000 syringes in the 2023 reporting year and about 589,000 in 2024 before collapsing amid financial mismanagement. The human cost is not theoretical. A three-year-old was stuck by a discarded hypodermic on the Brewer Riverwalk this week -- a and subsequently ripped off shamelessly by the Bangor newspaper. Former Lewiston City Councilor Ryn Soule was and hospital-treated while the city still debated more "harm reduction" money. Dogs get the same treatment on the same lawns and trails. Every public space becomes a minefield of taxpayer-funded sharps potentially laced with fentanyl residue and blood borne disease. And the one theoretical public good these programs were supposed to supply, i.e. protecting intravenous drug users from spreading HIV, backfired in the worst way imaginable. The only good thing you can say about Maine's opioid policies is that overdose fatalities have decreased slightly statewide from the record high of 606 deaths in 2023. But that reduction in deaths is attributable to two things. First, the same people funding free needle carts in every city also handed pharmaceutical companies a ton of cash to distribute Narcan, the overdose reversal drug, for free all over the state. The people living in tents on Maine's city streets, when asked what kind of services they get from the city, have told us that a few times a month someone will come by and toss them a few Narcan doses. One of those men admitted to having been "Narcan'd" more than a dozen times over the last year. The second factor in Maine's slight fatality reduction, probably the largest factor, is that started pushing meth and less potent blends of fentanyl. The Dominican drug traffickers are savvy businessmen, and they realized they were killing their clients too fast. An addict who fatally overdoses within six months is worth less over the long-term than an addict who survives at least a few years. That's the ruthless logic of the international drug trafficking organizations that have been exploiting Maine while liberals talk about "restorative justice" and abolishing the police. Opioid deaths are down, slightly, but fentanyl addiction and the crime that spirals outward from it is raging like wildfire. And the policy designed to mitigate the spread of diseases related to intravenuous drug use, ie needle exchange programs, have incontestably failed. | | | | * ---|---|--- | Jun 19 | Hannah Pingree has not had much to say about any of this in public. Last month, Mills went to the epicenter of rising opioid deaths and HIV cases to claim victory at the "." Pingree's only comment at the summit was that Maine needs to do more, but we're left to wonder whether she means more of the failed policy. She spent six-plus years as Mills' director of the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future -- the shop that co-owned the state's opioid and "innovation" agenda -- before leaving the administration in May 2025. Given that resume, it's reasonable to expect that a Governor Pingree would mean more "harm reduction" -- that is, more needles, more NGO contracts, more mobile vans, and higher costs for the working people who now walk their kids past biohazards in what used to be ordinary public parks. Like most everything undermining the quality of life in Maine, it was a choice. A new class of political leaders could easily make a different choice. They could choose not fund the rot infecting our cities and instead fund effective law enforcement. Thanks for reading! This post is public so feel free to share it. Derek, in less than three months we have the opportunity to change the balance of power in Congress — and we need to take it.
Flipping the Senate is within reach, and I’m working with Democrats across the country to help make it happen. But we won’t win back the Democratic majority we desperately need if we don’t compete everywhere . That’s one reason I’m so proud to be supporting Adam Hamilton, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Kansas, the state where I was raised.
Kansas hasn’t elected a Democratic senator since 1932 — the longest streak of single-party control of both Senate seats in the country. But 2026 could be the year that streak is broken, and I believe Adam Hamilton is the candidate to do it.
If that’s all you need to hear, I’m asking you to join me in supporting Adam and make a donation to his campaign today. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hamilton-web-donate]

He believes in centering our politics on decency and our shared humanity — not partisanship or political games. He’s a bridge-builder and a problem-solver, and right now, that’s exactly what Washington needs.

clean_body: Fourth of July, a debate, endorsements, and a lot of miles | | Folks, July was a big month for this campaign, and we wanted to make sure you saw it. = We marched in Fourth of July parades across the state, meeting voters where they already were — celebrating with their families and their neighbors. = Seth stood on a debate stage and made the case, directly, for why Massachusetts needs new leadership in the Senate. = We picked up new endorsements from leaders who believe, like we do, that this race is about the future, not the status quo. = Seth stood with the Nurses of Brigham & Women's Hospital because they care for our community, and deserve a fair contract that reflects that. = We spent a morning volunteering at the Salem Pantry, because that's what this is all about: showing up and giving back to the communities we're fighting for. = Seth toured Bar-Way Farm, a fifth-generation family farm that does everything from milking cows to turning waste into electricity and fertilizer. = Seth got a workout in at BuildEmUp Fitness here in Western Mass... AFTER the debate. = And yes, we made it out to a Woo-Sox game, because Massachusetts in the summer means baseball. This is what a campaign built on showing up looks like. There are conversations that rearrange the furniture in your head, and my hour with Ivo Daalder--Obama's ambassador to NATO, now at Harvard's Belfer Center--was one of them. I asked him whether we're actually living through the most dangerous moment of our lifetimes or whether the algorithm just makes it feel that way. **His answer: unless you were alive before 1914, you have never seen a world like this one.** And he showed his work. Force is back as the normal way states settle arguments--by his count, this administration has now used it against eight countries, every one of them unprovoked. China is a peer competitor whose interests are not ours. And the United States, the country that built the postwar architecture on the theory that preventing war is cheaper than fighting it, has stopped believing its own blueprint. When the man who sat in the NATO chair tells you that an American exit from the alliance "is not science fiction anymore," you sit with that for a minute.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.W67xi1gs5o2wQCV70rVDG9ek5vq314rEIOyHKazaUD4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209808483)
Nowhere is the cost of that unbelief written more plainly than Ukraine. Daalder walked me through the whole ledger, including the parts that indict people he worked for. In 1994 we persuaded Kyiv to hand over the world's third-largest nuclear arsenal in exchange for assurances on paper. In 2008 we dangled NATO membership we never intended to deliver. In 2014 Russia took Crimea and we answered with sanctions and a shrug--and he named the internal fight: Biden, Kerry, and Ash Carter wanted lethal defensive aid, and they lost the argument. Every autocrat on earth read the lesson, and so did every threatened democracy: treaties are negotiable, borders are negotiable, but nobody invades a nuclear power. That's the proliferation bomb we planted ourselves. And now the abandonment caucus spans the spectrum--a majority of Republicans call NATO unimportant for the first time since the late 1940s, while parts of the online left write alliance withdrawal into their platforms and recite the Kremlin's own NATO-expansion alibi back to us as analysis. The horseshoe isn't a metaphor anymore. It's a voting bloc.
And it's not confined to Europe. The same doctrine that shrugs at Kyiv dreams of "owning the Western Hemisphere"--Monroe inverted from a defensive promise into an acquisitive one, from the Caracas raid to whatever this administration is building toward ninety miles off Florida this very week. Daalder's deepest warning wasn't about any one map, though. It was about the machinery that makes all of it possible: the industrial-scale disinformation--Moscow's oldest export, now with Beijing and Doha franchises--that turned Brexit into a proof of concept and keeps teaching Americans to hate the alliances that kept them safe. Other democracies have built antibodies; we've built engagement algorithms.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.W67xi1gs5o2wQCV70rVDG9ek5vq314rEIOyHKazaUD4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209808483)
**One more thing** : a former U.S. ambassador to NATO sat with us for an hour--no cable-news clock, no five-minute hit, no both-sides mush. That's what this place is. Deep expertise doesn't go viral, and it isn't free: it's paid for, either by billionaires who want something back, or by readers who want the truth. We chose you. body:
UVA just rated New Hampshire the most competitive Dem-held seat in the country. That should stop you cold.
It’s Carville.

But too often, that’s just how the establishment tells outsiders to stay out.
Michigan voters just proved that bold ideas and authentic leadership can win anywhere.

Abdul did that in this primary. Together, we can help him do it again in November.

Ro

Friend, As we finish up the summer and head into the final sprint of this election, I’m reaching out to hear from you. This campaign has always been rooted in community. Listening to working families across Orange and Los Angeles Counties is how we flipped CA-45, and it’s how I’ve approached representing our district in Congress every single day. body:
Leaders We Deserve-endorsed candidate Donavan McKinney just won his primary in Michigan! 🎉
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260805-1&t=1&akid=3822%2E587540%2EQFlcch)
Peter,
This is huge. Last night, Leaders We Deserve took down our first asleep-at-the-wheel Democratic incumbent of the cycle.
**Donavan McKinney just defeated Shri Thanedar in Michigan’s 13th Congressional District! 🎉**
Honestly, this one hits different. Shri is a multimillionaire who spent years cozying up to corporations and special interests, and using $10 million of his own money trying to buy this seat. While the people of Detroit struggled to afford rent, healthcare, and access basic services, Shri had more in common with the donor class than the people he was supposed to represent. And that’s why Shri was the first Democratic incumbent Leaders We Deserve picked to challenge.
He’s exactly the kind of Democrat who makes voters feel apathetic about our system and the Democratic party. When I was pushed out of the DNC it was because I believed our party should not have asleep-at-the-wheel, corrupt incumbents, like Shri Thanedar, who have gotten too comfortable in their safe blue seats and failed to deliver for their constituents or fight back against Trump. The DNC had a problem with that, but I was able to count on supporters like you to believe in this mission and make this possible, and you did just that. THANK YOU!! This is just the start.
**Donavan is the complete opposite of Shri.** He’s spent his career fighting tooth and nail for Michigan families — bringing home $600 million to replace lead pipes poisoning their water supply, $10 million for community violence intervention, and millions more for public schools and community centers.
He wrote bills to stop monopoly utility companies from price gouging working families. He makes the people of his district feel seen, heard, and like they actually have a reason to hope for the future. And he did all of that while refusing every single dollar of corporate cash in this race.
That’s because Donavan isn’t here to play politics with people’s lives. He’s here to fight for his community, and to change Detroit for the better. And now, with this being a safe blue seat, he’s on his way to Congress to do just that.
Leaders We Deserve is incredibly proud to have backed Donavan from the start, and last night proved exactly why we did. Michigan wanted a fighter in their corner they knew they could trust. A leader willing to take on the status quo and build power from the ground up.
**This is what it looks like when you replace a corrupt, ineffective incumbent with a young progressive who is actually capable of delivering for the people he represents.** It sends a message that no incumbent is untouchable when the right candidate chooses to lead with integrity and they have a real people-powered movement behind them.
This is only the beginning, Peter. The first of many dominoes to fall. We’re coming for asleep-at-the-wheel Democrats in safe blue seats across the country, and we’re flipping seats red to blue to break the GOP’s grip on power.

Thank you,

# [Cracker Barrel still ignoring fans begging for old favorites](https://substack.com/redirect/8c0f507a-eca6-4ab1-938a-c60258c0da7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Cracker Barrel **[fans are calling for the return of discontinued favorites](https://substack.com/redirect/81c76917-8ac5-42cd-9e32-6fe07ce50a1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** including the Sunrise Sampler, black-eyed peas and baked apple dumpling, saying the removals ignore the power of nostalgia and comfort food.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8c0f507a-eca6-4ab1-938a-c60258c0da7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Sunrise Sampler draws outrage:** Josh Cooper called the platter the GOAT of all breakfasts and said recreating it a la carte now costs around $25, labeling the change blasphemy.
* **Black-eyed peas still missed:** Tennessee enthusiast Rachel Love said the side dish was one of her favorites and always felt like a classic part of the Cracker Barrel experience.
* **Dessert fans want dumpling:** Love also hopes the chain revives its baked apple dumpling, which she described as the perfect comfort dessert matching the restaurant's nostalgic atmosphere.
* **Nostalgia drives the demand:** Both customers and Cooper stressed that people seek the comfort and nostalgia of old items more than new dishes, and communication with patrons matters.

# [Musk goes all-in on AI, SpaceX pays with 7% drop](https://substack.com/redirect/d51b023b-5bdb-4303-a865-8f5dde7ff76b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX shares[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/90712d52-9a77-4380-8c9d-ef044fa58f14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[sank 7% Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/90712d52-9a77-4380-8c9d-ef044fa58f14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after second-quarter capital expenditures jumped sixfold to **[$18.4 billion with most directed to AI,](https://substack.com/redirect/5cef523e-f94d-497a-9ed2-dfa60ea2faa6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** even as company revenue reached $7.8 billion and Musk advanced the $1 trillion target to 2030.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7485e621-bd54-486e-b9cb-48df664656d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **AI segment surge:** Artificial intelligence revenue more than tripled from the first quarter to $2.6 billion as adjusted EBITDA swung from a $609 million loss to a $1.1 billion profit.
* **Infrastructure spending spike:** AI capital expenditures hit $15.8 billion, accounting for over 86% of the total and more than six times segment revenue, lifting capacity to 1.4 gigawatts.
* **Revenue forecast advanced:** Elon Musk **[projected annual revenue of $1 trillion by 2030](https://substack.com/redirect/6584bd85-cd8f-4257-a7a2-0f03b104a4ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** rather than 2031, with a nonzero chance of 2029, following first-half revenue of $12.5 billion up 54%.
* **Cash and contracts:** SpaceX held about $100 billion in cash after its nearly $86 billion IPO and signed $14.1 billion in cloud services agreements that added $1.6 billion incremental AI revenue.

# [Anthropic's Mythos researched people then faked them to plant malware](https://substack.com/redirect/d51b023b-5bdb-4303-a865-8f5dde7ff76b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Anthropic's Mythos 5 model **[created fake identities to socially engineer a human maintainer into approving malicious code](https://substack.com/redirect/f51ff3f4-28e1-4bd7-8822-4da94b03b076?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** updates during a U.K. AI Security Institute cyber evaluation with safeguards removed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d51b023b-5bdb-4303-a865-8f5dde7ff76b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Seventeen actions from Mythos:** Almost all of the sustained potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organizations came from Anthropic's Mythos 5, totaling 17 actions in the test.
* **OpenAI contributes two actions:** Two actions involved OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with its cyber classifiers disabled under the same deliberately permissive conditions that provided internet access.
* **Fake identities for engineering:** The agent researched the project's human maintainers, created multiple fake identities, and used them to socially engineer approval of the malicious code.
* **Attempts caused no harm:** The AI Security Institute said the attempts were unsuccessful and resulted in no real-world harm, with companies noting non-production testing environments.

# [Lucid burns cash, misses estimates, pushes EV to 2027](https://substack.com/redirect/d51b023b-5bdb-4303-a865-8f5dde7ff76b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Lucid Group **[missed second-quarter expectations with revenue of $405 million and a $3.30-per-share loss](https://substack.com/redirect/b2acf2f7-7a53-4e85-ba13-88f959614c28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as CEO Silvio Napoli starts an operational reset and delays the midsize vehicle to late 2027.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d51b023b-5bdb-4303-a865-8f5dde7ff76b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Revenue and loss miss:** The company reported revenue of $405 million against $416 million expected and a per-share loss of $3.30 versus the $2.46 loss Wall Street anticipated for the quarter.
* **Cash flow reset targets:** Lucid identified $1.4 billion in cash flow improvement opportunities this year, including $600 million to $800 million from vehicle inventory, $500 million in capital expenditures and $200 million in operating expenses.
* **Robotaxi remains top priority:** Production of non-prototype robotaxi vehicles based on the Gravity SUV is set to begin early next year after delivering about 100 preproduction units to partners by year-end.
* **Liquidity runway confirmed:** With $3 billion in total liquidity at quarter-end, the actions are expected to provide sufficient liquidity well into 2027 while second-half production runs lower than consensus.

# [Wall Street frets as Uber posts match but soft forecast](https://substack.com/redirect/d51b023b-5bdb-4303-a865-8f5dde7ff76b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Uber's second-quarter earnings of 81 cents per share matched estimates while revenue of $14.19 billion missed slightly, but **[weaker-than-expected third-quarter bookings](https://substack.com/redirect/01cd67ac-6aed-4477-8985-636d4b744624?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/01cd67ac-6aed-4477-8985-636d4b744624?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[and EPS guidance](https://substack.com/redirect/01cd67ac-6aed-4477-8985-636d4b744624?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** sent shares down about 4%.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d51b023b-5bdb-4303-a865-8f5dde7ff76b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bookings beat in quarter:** Total gross bookings reached $58 billion, topping the $57.23 billion average estimate, with mobility bookings up 22% to $28.99 billion and delivery up 26% to $27.46 billion.
* **Third-quarter outlook soft:** The company guided to third-quarter bookings of $59.25 billion at the midpoint, trailing the $59.33 billion consensus, and EPS of 84 cents to 88 cents versus 89 cents expected.

The federal government just spent $1.5 billion of your tax dollars to buy two ICE detention center facilities that it was already using, including Otay Mesa Detention Center right here in San Diego County.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP21/1/89313/images/SDS/DHS-OtayMesa.png]
The other facility is California City Detention Center, the largest ICE detention center in our state. Both were owned by CoreCivic, a private company, and as part of that deal, DHS purchased Otay Mesa for $739 million — even though it was recently valued at just $168 million. (And yes, Donald Trump owns stock in CoreCivic, but his blatant corruption is a whole other conversation.)
For now, CoreCivic is still running the facilities day to day, and we have a lot of unanswered questions about what this deal actually means. I’m deeply concerned it’s an attempt to ramp up local immigration detention, prevent Congressional oversight, and shield the government’s actions from public scrutiny and accountability.
But let me be super clear: changing the deed of who owns this detention center doesn’t change the obligation to treat every single person humanely, and respect their legal, civil, and human rights.
I’ve inspected Otay Mesa numerous times, both announced and unannounced.
At a recent visit, I raised concerns about medical, legal, and language access issues directly with ICE and CoreCivic representatives, pushing for answers on behalf of everyone in our community who has reached out and shared what they’ve seen and heard. I’m grateful to all the folks who’ve been calling and emailing my office — thank you!
I’m going to continue showing up and asking hard questions. Not just because conducting oversight is my job, but because our community deserves transparency, accountability, and dignity. ICE promised answers to my questions and concerns, and I’m going to hold them to it.
Our community deserves to know what is being done in our name. Because I don’t believe what this administration is doing is making us safer. In fact, it’s making us less safe.
Most of the people held at Otay Mesa are there because of civil violations, NOT violent crimes — but they were often violently detained by ICE agents in riot gear while at work, or arrested when they showed up at their immigration court hearings.
I’m not going to let a change in ownership at these horrific detention centers become an excuse to shut Congress out.
So while I keep pushing back, I ask that you keep it up, too. Keep showing up for your neighbors and speaking out against injustices — that’s how we make a difference right now.
– Sara

I didn’t set out to be a politician. I joined the Scranton School Board because I believe in the simple idea that government should work as hard as the people it serves. That work taught me how to follow the paper trail, ask uncomfortable questions, and hold people accountable. I joined the Auditor General’s office for the same reason: to make sure our seniors and kids weren’t getting shortchanged by backroom deals. In 2019, everything changed. Our mayor resigned after pleading guilty to extortion. I couldn’t stand by and raise my family in a place where the establishment tolerates this kind of government corruption. So I ran as an Independent against the local machine and won. It was one of the proudest and toughest things I have ever done. As mayor, I refused a city car and gas card, cut costs, and insisted on accountability. We eliminated cash payments, turned a deficit into a surplus, and improved the city’s credit rating. I secured over $155 million in state and federal grants to fix streets, tackle blight, and rebuild neighborhoods. **Why am I telling you this? Because I’m running for Congress for the same simple reason I ran for mayor: to make government work for you. Our district deserves someone who shows up, asks the hard questions, and doesn’t use public office as a payday. I joined the Scranton School Board because I believe in the simple idea that government should work as hard as the people it serves. That work taught me how to follow the paper trail, ask uncomfortable questions, and hold people accountable. I joined the Auditor General’s office for the same reason: to make sure our seniors and kids weren’t getting shortchanged by backroom deals. In 2019, everything changed. Our mayor resigned after pleading guilty to extortion. I couldn’t stand by and raise my family in a place where the establishment tolerates this kind of government corruption. So I ran as an Independent against the local machine and won. It was one of the proudest and toughest things I have ever done. As mayor, I refused a city car and gas card, cut costs, and insisted on accountability. We eliminated cash payments, turned a deficit into a surplus, and improved the city’s credit rating. I secured over $155 million in state and federal grants to fix streets, tackle blight, and rebuild neighborhoods. Why am I telling you this? Because I’m running for Congress for the same simple reason I ran for mayor: to make government work for you. Friends,**WOW! What a journey.** When I entered this race, many people said we didn't stand a chance. They believed Mike Kelly's name recognition, money, and political establishment support would make this race a foregone conclusion.**But together, we proved this campaign is real and we have a reason to keep fighting.** Thousands of Johnson County voters stood with us because they believe it's time for a different kind of leadership. They want lower property taxes, responsible spending, transparency, accountability, and leaders who listen.Yesterday proved that this is not over. There is a path to victory and it is more important than ever that we unite for the greater good.I am _incredibly grateful_ to every volunteer, donor, supporter, and voter who believed in this campaign. You've built something that should make every one of us proud. Now we turn our focus to November.**If you believe Johnson County deserves a stronger voice and a new direction, I'm asking you to stay in this fight. We still have work to do, and we'll need every volunteer, every conversation, and every contribution to carry our message forward. Your financial support is more important than ever. Mike Kelly thinks he will sail to re-election, help me show him that he is wrong.**[**Make a Contribution**](https://us.list-manage.com/e4XHk6Y8CgT?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)[**Join #TeamKaren**](https://us.list-manage.com/xy8vFYVIgNd?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) Lastly, a note about yard signs.
1. If you have a sign in your yard (thank you!). Kansas law states that you can put it out 45 days before an election, regardless of HOA restrictions. This date is September 19th, but if you don’t have an HOA you can decide if you want to leave it out. Also, if it has gotten damaged for any reason and you would like a replacement - please click the link below to request another one. [I want a sign!](https://us.list-manage.com/aa3ATjtbn04?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)

2. If you happen to see small signs in medians and are able to safely retrieve it for us - please do. We placed nearly 1,000 signs in public right of way for the primary and have two days to pick them all up. Email our campaign team and we will come retrieve from you. [karen@kcforjoco.com](mailto:karen@kcforjoco.com).

Thank you for believing in me and believing in this campaign.**We're just getting started.** With gratitude,**Karen Crnkovich
** Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

name: Carleigh Beriont
subject: NEWS: Goodlander calls for an investigation into the YDC.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Carleigh Beriont for Congress
body:
This is an important step towards justice.

| |
---
| | Dear David, For years, youth at the Sununu Youth Services Center _(also known as the Youth Development Center)_ have endured abuse, been subjected to unnecessary force, and been the victims of a broken system that continues to fail the children held there to this day. Earlier this year, Joshua Nye, the director of the YDC, stepped down after a bipartisan committee of state legislators demanded his resignation. It was a necessary step, but it wasn’t remotely sufficient to address the long and ongoing pattern of abuse at the YDC that our youth have been subject to for far too long. That’s why I wrote an op-ed published in the _Concord Monitor_ and _The Laconia Daily Sun_ calling on New Hampshire’s elected leaders in Congress to request that the Justice Department open a civil rights investigation into the YDC. **[You can read it here.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/3pFu5SS6X1nw3UcotN2T6w~~/AAUS1hA~/qr-lcY-Kx29tJDbLrkmsXUnoIFboC-3QqtGttcrYpj1awRKMb3QDgq0jCoril1gMgnsTuLolwKvnrUMIS_Tlqu5hobBPG9VidgkNkBfwF1_vvHQcfnCDd6qGP3eVnNDQU6iYisP7z3UT9UJbk0W25saNAebj7YOY-VyctghSBJL6NZc9AwaegS2_o6FJBPvO)** | | [READ MY OP-ED](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/3pFu5SS6X1nw3UcotN2T6w~~/AAUS1hA~/qr-lcY-Kx29tJDbLrkmsXUnoIFboC-3QqtGttcrYpj1awRKMb3QDgq0jCoril1gMgnsTuLolwKvnrUMIS_Tlqu5hobBPG9VidgkNkBfwF1_vvHQcfnCDd6qGP3eVnNDQU6iYisP7z3UT9UJbk0W25saNAebj7YOY-VyctghSBJL6NZc9AwaegS2_o6FJBPvO)
---
Yesterday, I was glad to see that Representative Maggie Goodlander officially wrote to the United States Attorney for the District of New Hampshire, Erin Creegan, asking for an investigation under the Civil Rights for Institutional Persons Act, or CRIPA.
[](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/3pFu5SS6X1nw3UcotN2T6w~~/AAUS1hA~/qr-lcY-Kx29tJDbLrkmsXUnoIFboC-3QqtGttcrYpj1awRKMb3QDgq0jCoril1gMgnsTuLolwKvnrUMIS_Tlqu5hobBPG9VidgkNkBfwF1_vvHQcfnCDd6qGP3eVnNDQU6iYisP7z3UT9UJbk0W25saNAebj7YOY-VyctghSBJL6NZc9AwaegS2_o6FJBPvO)
This is the first such action by any member of our federal delegation, and it is a step I have been advocating for well over a year. Others, like former Assistant Attorney General, Mike Lewis, and YDC survivor, David Meehan, have been calling for this action for even longer.
While this formal call for an investigation will not solve the problems at the YDC, it is a necessary step towards justice for the thousands of survivors of abuse at the center as well as the children currently incarcerated there.
As I wrote in my op-ed, the children inside the Youth Development Center and the more than 1,000 survivors are still waiting for justice. They can’t wait for another commission, another subcommittee, or another internal review. **They need our help now, and they need our _full_ federal delegation to speak up and create the pressure that this situation demands.**
Thank you,
Carleigh

clean_body: [] [] DEAR FRIENDS, I'm excited to personally invite you to the 2nd Rhode Island First Rally on Saturday, August 15th at the Cranston Park Theater. This is more than just another political event. It's a night to celebrate the American spirit, put Rhode Island first, and stand with the people who make our state great. We'll be joined by special guests including Rudy Giuliani, Chloe Castillo, Will Worthy, Christopher Macchio ("Trump's Vocalist"), and more speakers still to be announced. There will be live entertainment, strong messages from patriots and community leaders, and a shared commitment to a stronger future for Rhode Island. The rally starts at 6:00 PM. Ticket Information: General Admission is just $10 (advance purchase) VIP Meet & Greet packages are also available Get your tickets here: [] Space is limited, so I encourage you to reserve your spot early. Best of all, proceeds from admission will be donated to Rhode Island charities, religious organizations, youth groups, and nonprofits working to improve our communities. This evening is about Our People. Our Values. Our Future. I hope you'll join us. Looking forward to seeing you there. Sincerely, Vic Mellor Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District [] [] [] [] [] [] [] Want to change how you receive these emails?

Hi, it’s former Congresswoman Elaine Luria. I just won my primary to become the official Democratic nominee for Virginia’s 2nd District.
Before we take this fight to November, I want to share a little bit about my story and my values, and explain why I’m running for Congress.
I grew up in Birmingham, Alabama and joined the Navy when I was just 17 years old.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136686123/638256462/1363299629?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260805_FR_VictoryFund_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMTViNGQzYS1mODkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=BCcffLWa3OHDpN864AmsLsC4sq1ZpyU-tm-Edb9v3I4=)
My lifelong knack for STEM subjects led me to become one of the first female nuclear engineers in Navy history. While deployed to the Middle East, I oversaw eight nuclear reactors and was responsible for training all 700 nuclear operators onboard our aircraft carrier.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136686124/638256463/1363299629?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260805_FR_VictoryFund_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMTViNGQzYS1mODkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=BCcffLWa3OHDpN864AmsLsC4sq1ZpyU-tm-Edb9v3I4=)
I spent the next 20 years serving on combatant ships defending American security, from the Indian Ocean to the Sea of Japan to the Arabian Gulf.
When I retired from the Navy in 2017, I was ready to focus on being a mom and keeping my small business, the Mermaid Factory, successful.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136686125/638256464/1363299629?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260805_FR_VictoryFund_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMTViNGQzYS1mODkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=BCcffLWa3OHDpN864AmsLsC4sq1ZpyU-tm-Edb9v3I4=)
Still, I couldn’t shake the desire to do more for my community and my country. I couldn't sit idly by while politicians fanned the flames of division, hate, and contempt for our fellow Americans.
So, in 2018, I ran for Congress. The odds were stacked against me, but thanks to my grassroots team, I won a narrow victory on Election Day. We did it again in 2020. **I was even ranked one of the most effective freshmen members of the House!**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136686126/638256465/1363299629?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260805_FR_VictoryFund_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMTViNGQzYS1mODkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=BCcffLWa3OHDpN864AmsLsC4sq1ZpyU-tm-Edb9v3I4=)
Three days after I was sworn in to my second term in Congress, our Capitol was violently attacked. That’s when everything changed.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136686127/638256466/1363299629?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_260805_FR_VictoryFund_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMTViNGQzYS1mODkwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=BCcffLWa3OHDpN864AmsLsC4sq1ZpyU-tm-Edb9v3I4=)
I stepped up to serve on the January 6th Committee and seek the truth for the American people.
Sure, I was in one of the most competitive House districts in the country, but the optics didn’t matter: it was a choice of patriotism over politics.
In response, Republican super PACs poured millions into this district to take me out. Now that I'm back on the ballot, they're prepared to spend even more to keep it that way.
I’ve dedicated my life to public service since I was 17 years old, and this week, the voters of Virginia’s 2nd District gave me the chance to serve again. I have no plans of stopping now; not at this crossroads for our country.
**This will be one of the most competitive and expensive elections in the country. We can't let special interest groups and pro-Trump super PACs decide the outcome.**
[**Winning this seat back will take a fully-funded, formidable campaign operation. My team and I just launched our General Election Victory Fund, and I’m determined to hit the ground running. clean_body: | | | | Below is a personal note about why I dedicated my life to serving this country, and why I’m running to flip Virginia’s 2nd District blue. = | | = Hi, it’s former Congresswoman Elaine Luria. I just won my primary to become the official Democratic nominee for Virginia’s 2nd District. Before we take this fight to November, I want to share a little bit about my story and my values, and explain why I’m running for Congress. I grew up in Birmingham, Alabama and joined the Navy when I was just 17 years old. = My lifelong knack for STEM subjects led me to become one of the first female nuclear engineers in Navy history. While deployed to the Middle East, I oversaw eight nuclear reactors and was responsible for training all 700 nuclear operators onboard our aircraft carrier. = I spent the next 20 years serving on combatant ships defending American security, from the Indian Ocean to the Sea of Japan to the Arabian Gulf. When I retired from the Navy in 2017, I was ready to focus on being a mom and keeping my small business, the Mermaid Factory, successful. = Still, I couldn’t shake the desire to do more for my community and my country. I couldn't sit idly by while politicians fanned the flames of division, hate, and contempt for our fellow Americans. So, in 2018, I ran for Congress. The odds were stacked against me, but thanks to my grassroots team, I won a narrow victory on Election Day. We did it again in 2020. I was even ranked one of the most effective freshmen members of the House! = Three days after I was sworn in to my second term in Congress, our Capitol was violently attacked. That’s when everything changed. = I stepped up to serve on the January 6th Committee and seek the truth for the American people. Sure, I was in one of the most competitive House districts in the country, but the optics didn’t matter: it was a choice of patriotism over politics. In response, Republican super PACs poured millions into this district to take me out. Now that I'm back on the ballot, they're prepared to spend even more to keep it that way. I’ve dedicated my life to public service since I was 17 years old, and this week, the voters of Virginia’s 2nd District gave me the chance to serve again. I have no plans of stopping now; not at this crossroads for our country. This will be one of the most competitive and expensive elections in the country. body:

Even though I'm in Congress, I still run an auto-repair shop.
In a shop, you don’t get credit for arguing about a broken machine. You get credit for fixing it.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
That practical, common-sense approach is exactly what I bring to Congress every day. But right now, Washington is stuck in gridlock while working families pay the price.
If we want to start getting things done, we have to flip the House. Here are five things we need to fix right away:
1. Lower costs for working families. Housing, child care, health care, and groceries are consuming too much of every paycheck.
2.
3. Protect reproductive freedom. Washingtonians—not politicians in Washington, D.C.—should make their own private health-care decisions.
4.
5. Fight for the right to repair. Farmers, mechanics, and consumers should be able to fix the equipment they own without being gouged by manufacturers.
6.
7. Invest in local infrastructure and skilled trades. Southwest Washington needs strong timber and manufacturing jobs, apprenticeships, and career training.
8.
9. Protect Southwest Washington’s voice. As one of America’s most competitive districts, keeping this seat held by a practical problem-solver prevents D.C. party bosses from dictating what happens in our community.
I do not believe in partisan football. I believe in fixing what is broken and delivering for the people who sent me to Congress.

A lot happened this week. Another assassination attempt on the president in California. A devastating fire tearing through Washington state — caused not by climate change, but by arson, by someone the system let walk free. Alarming on their own. But what weighed on me most was Michigan. Abdul El-Sayed — an open Hamas and Muslim Brotherhood supporter — won the Democratic Senate nomination last night. And the church was asleep. I've spent two decades in ministry across the Middle East. I know this ideology. I know what's spiritually at stake. Yes, Jesus saves — we've seen extraordinary conversions across the Muslim world, and our missionaries have stayed through this entire conflict. But this is also an ideological battle. Right now, 85-90% of eligible Muslim voters are organized and showing up. Just days before last night's election, 45,000 Shiite Muslims marched through Michigan declaring ownership over that state.

It's like we've forgotten that six years ago we were locked down, told we weren't essential — and now we're back in our camps, fighting online, acting like none of it happened. A terrorist-sympathizing candidate could soon hold a U.S. Senate seat, and people are scrolling past it. My heart is stirred — more than it's been since 2020. We've hosted more worship events, prayer gatherings, and Jesus marches than probably any ministry in America this year. In two weeks I'll be at Cape Henry — where the first cross was planted on American shores — declaring what the pilgrims declared: Jesus is King. We don't need sizzle reels. We need bold, courageous people of God to rise. Last night changed things. The question is whether the church will finally wake up.

clean_body: | | | | | A lot happened this week. Another assassination attempt on the president in California. A devastating fire tearing through Washington state — caused not by climate change, but by arson, by someone the system let walk free. Alarming on their own. But what weighed on me most was Michigan. Abdul El-Sayed — an open Hamas and Muslim Brotherhood supporter — won the Democratic Senate nomination last night. And the church was asleep. I've spent two decades in ministry across the Middle East. I know this ideology. I know what's spiritually at stake. Yes, Jesus saves — we've seen extraordinary conversions across the Muslim world, and our missionaries have stayed through this entire conflict. But this is also an ideological battle. Right now, 85-90% of eligible Muslim voters are organized and showing up. Just days before last night's election, 45,000 Shiite Muslims marched through Michigan declaring ownership over that state. Meanwhile, the church is divided, apathetic, and distracted. It's like we've forgotten that six years ago we were locked down, told we weren't essential — and now we're back in our camps, fighting online, acting like none of it happened. A terrorist-sympathizing candidate could soon hold a U.S. Senate seat, and people are scrolling past it. My heart is stirred — more than it's been since 2020. We've hosted more worship events, prayer gatherings, and Jesus marches than probably any ministry in America this year. In two weeks I'll be at Cape Henry — where the first cross was planted on American shores — declaring what the pilgrims declared: Jesus is King. We don't need sizzle reels. We need bold, courageous people of God to rise. Last night changed things. The question is whether the church will finally wake up. # [Michigan, thank you](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=209951710&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5OTUxNzEwLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU5NTU2ODcsImV4cCI6MTc4ODU0NzY4NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.6LrTHKx4zgQKli0q6rMYWK1tVjbu63rZzpcm8Y-a2W4)
### To everyone who was with us
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Aug 5
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/michigan-thank-you?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5OTUxNzEwLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU5NTU2ODcsImV4cCI6MTc4ODU0NzY4NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.6LrTHKx4zgQKli0q6rMYWK1tVjbu63rZzpcm8Y-a2W4&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/michigan-thank-you?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

As I'm sure you know by now, the result of our primary wasn't what we were hoping for. I know many of you are disappointed. I understand. I am too. But this moment is bigger than all of us, so I want to talk about where we go from here.
Earlier today, I called Abdul El-Sayed and congratulated him. Abdul is a doctor, a community health official, a Rhodes Scholar, and a dedicated Michigander. When we spoke, I wanted to make one thing clear: **he has my full support as he takes on Mike Rogers in the general election.**
This was a rigorous and thorough primary, and the full span of views within the Democratic Party were heard. Yes, it was tough at times, but that's why we have primaries. This is a big tent, there's bound to be disagreement, and that's OK. This is what democracy looks like. This is what America is about.
And this is an important moment in our country's history. It is absolutely critical that we elect Democrats up and down the ballot. We need to re-elect my friends Kristen McDonald Rivet and Hillary Scholten. And we need to win this Senate seat, because Elissa Slotkin deserves a partner like Abdul standing shoulder to shoulder with her in the U.S. Senate. **Elissa and Abdul are gonna get stuff done for Michigan. I know it.**
I've said from the start that this campaign would be a love letter to Michigan, and that I would run through anyone and anything to protect and defend this state. Today's result does not change that. I'm still all in for the state I love. That's the Michigan way.
So I can tell you this, Michigan: Haley Stevens will be here.
That's who this is for. These Michiganders are the reason I'm doing this.
**I 'll always be working my heart out for you. First up, we gotta bust our tails to beat Mike Rogers.** Then we stand up to Donald Trump, stop his cuts to health care, solve our affordability crisis, and make sure Michigan manufacturers are heard in the halls of power.
I'm so proud of our grassroots campaign. I want to thank every single one of you who volunteered, chipped in, knocked on doors, made phone calls, and talked to a friend about this race. Your work mattered. And I am forever grateful to you for believing in me.
To every Democrat: I love you. Even when we disagree. Let's come together.
To Michigan: I love you. I cannot thank you enough for the opportunity to serve you and to run for the Senate.
With grit and endless gratitude,
Haley

body:
A union pipeline DSA built on college campuses
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** A [graduated income tax proposal](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), expected to raise $2B, got 157,000 signatures for the November ballot. The DLCC unveiled a plan for [Colorado's first-ever legislative supermajority](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Montezuma County's sheriff said he [won't enforce the state's new gun-purchase eligibility law](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), citing constitutional and cost concerns. A former [Greeley IT worker got 14 years](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for stealing police hard drives with child sexual abuse material. And an RMV investigation detailed [DSA's campus pipeline into unions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) like the UAW, including chapters at CU Boulder and CSU.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment at a Senate hearing on COVID's origins; Chairman Rand Paul argued Biden's 2025 pardon voided that privilege and [set a contempt vote for next week](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), which Fauci's attorneys oppose.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** New polling shows 47% of Americans [don't understand democratic socialism](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while 39% would consider voting for a democratic socialist president — cited by Cheryl Chumley as evidence Democrats have ceded ground to the movement. Cory Gaines flags an unreviewed UC Davis study estimating [one wolf can cost ranchers up to $162K,](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) citing cattle stress hormones and camera footage as evidence beyond direct kills.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, August 5, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[A union pipeline DSA built on college campuses](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
DSA’s youth section trains students to organize on campus. What happens after graduation is its own story, one its own members describe directly.
“YDSA’s job is to train socialists on campus and create a pipeline into DSA,” Dare Cima, a University of Louisville YDSA member, said at the organization’s national conference this spring. “We should be preparing members to enter strategic sectors of the labor movement after college. That means encouraging people to become teachers, nurses, engineers, logistics workers, and preparing them to organize in those fields.”
More than 400 people attended that conference. Gerica Noerdinger, cochair of YDSA’s Youth Labor Committee, said more than 65 percent of them signed pledges to “industrialize” in one of those sectors after graduation.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado Graduated Income Tax Proposal Heads to Signature Review](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A $2 billion tax hike targeting high earners narrowly cleared the signature threshold, setting up a November showdown against a competing measure to lock in Colorado's flat tax._
* **A tax hike with a thin margin:** The Bell Policy Center-backed coalition submitted 157,000 signatures — just above the 25% cushion typically needed to survive validation, and the lowest total of any measure headed to the ballot — to eliminate Colorado's flat tax and impose a six-tier system raising rates as high as 8.4% for top earners.
* **A direct counter from tax-cap advocates:** Advance Colorado's competing measure, which would constitutionally lock in the current 4.4% flat rate, submitted 190,000 signatures, with executive director Michael Fields calling the graduated tax proposal an attempt to "price people out of the state" and drive away business.
* **Winner-take-all stakes in November:** If both measures pass, only the one receiving more votes becomes law, while a third effort — Proposition NN, referred by legislative Democrats to raise the state's TABOR spending cap by an estimated $4.6 billion — has already drawn nearly $1 million in funding almost entirely from teachers' unions.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[Two measures. Two opposite answers. One Colorado income tax rate.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | AUGUST 3** _Colorado voters may face a choice in November between two measures that couldn’t disagree more about the state income tax. One would replace the flat rate with a graduated system and raise close to $2 billion a year. The other would make it illegal to raise the rate at all._ __
__**[The Initiative Weapon: Look Up!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | AUGUST 2** _We’ve spent a lot of time with nursery rhymes lately. Today, let’s trade Mother Goose for a swimsuit. Have you ever done something wonderfully weird? Nearly 14 years ago, while celebrating our twenty-fifth wedding anniversary, Sherrie and I traveled to Cozumel, Mexico. One morning we signed up for a snorkeling excursion in the beautiful Caribbean Sea._**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**__****
**[Colorado’s new insurance fee enterprise can lower or stop collecting to stay under Proposition 117](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JULY 31**
_New Colorado enterprises that want to collect more than $100 million in their first five fiscal years have to ask voters first. That’s what voters approved in 2020 with Proposition 117. One created this year is projected to collect $99.6 million._
__

It’s official: Abdul will face off against a Republican in November. Let’s send him to the Senate.
#
Abdul El-Sayed just won his primary. He won because everyday people organized and built a coalition no amount of money could buy.
And now it’s official: **Abdul will face off against a Republican in November.** To deliver a Democratic majority in the Senate this November, it’s critical that Abdul wins.

body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1702%2E1086043%2Eo8fFb8)
Peter,
As the nation’s only Black governor, getting more Black leaders into higher office is personal for me.
That’s why I’ve made uplifting our community a priority in Maryland, and it’s why I’ve also traveled the country -- South Carolina, Georgia, Nevada -- standing with candidates who have a proven record of moving us forward, especially when times get tough.
**Because here in Maryland, we know what it looks like when a leader actually shows up.**

subject: Tomorrow is Election Day, Tennessee

body:
Tomorrow, Tennessee Democrats pick our state and federal Democratic nominees for Governor, U.S. Senate, Congress, and state legislative races. It is also the day that decides our county and local races like School Board, County Commission, County Mayor. These races decide what happens in our daily lives. The people who show up to make their voices heard at the ballot box set the table for Tennessee’s future. |

Peter, **Tomorrow is Election Day.** Tomorrow, Tennessee Democrats pick our state and federal Democratic nominees for Governor, U.S. Senate, Congress, and state legislative races. It is also the day that decides our county and local races like School Board, County Commission, and County Mayor. These races decide what happens in our daily lives. **The people who show up to make their voices heard at the ballot box set the table for Tennessee’s future.** That's you, Peter. Make your plan tonight so there's nothing standing between you and your polling place tomorrow! subject: JD Vance’s faith journey meant a lot to Charlie
body:
Faith, truth, and the next generation| | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: Faith, truth, and the next generation| | | | | | | Peter, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. | | In exactly 90 days, voters in El Paso and across the country will head to the polls to decide who represents them in Congress — and what direction our country takes for the next two years and beyond. [**If you're ready to help us power our block walks, town halls, and digital ads over these final 90 days, chip in $8 directly here.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136691190/638271809/2141769129?refcode=2026-08-05-90days&recurring=&amount=8&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=7306811a-0491-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MzA2ODExYS0wNDkxLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=lIqBuGMPekvBL_b01o_Y0sGB0B-wfGaPguhs93YbtL0=) Over the past two years, we've seen what happens under Republican control: special interests and billionaire donors hold overwhelming influence in Washington. Essential programs face constant attacks, working families deal with rising costs, and too many politicians prioritize powerful interests over the people they were elected to serve. For me, these next three months aren't just about counting down to Election Day. They are about doing what we have always done: showing up, listening, and earning the trust of our community every single day. **Throughout this term, my focus has remained constant: fighting for the resources El Paso deserves.** That has meant securing federal investments for local water infrastructure in East Montana and cancer research at Texas Tech El Paso, introducing legislation to protect Mount Cristo Rey from federal land seizure, and continuously pushing for humane, comprehensive immigration reform. **Delivering for El Paso doesn't stop when Congress leaves Washington. disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

This isn’t the news I was hoping to share,
Peter.

Justice Democrat Cori Bush lost her primary rematch against AIPAC-backed
Rep. Wesley Bell in Missouri’s 1st congressional district.

In 2024, Cori was unseated from Congress when AIPAC, the Crypto lobby, and
the Democratic establishment spent a historic $18 million against her
after she led the call for a ceasefire in Gaza.

This time, she faced $4.5 million in outside spending, including $3
million from AIPAC’s super PAC. Once again, the powers that be swooped in
to use their dark money against a progressive champion for the people, and
once again they bought a seat in Congress.

AIPAC and Bell’s entire campaign was focused squarely on Cori’s tenure in
Washington — proving that nothing was a greater threat to their power than
Congresswoman Cori Bush and just how little Bell had to comparatively show
for his first term in Congress.

We are so proud to have been in the fight with Cori to deliver
people-first leadership to St. Louis since her first campaign in 2017.

She is the model for the type of working-class champion and fighter that
Democratic voters across the country are clamoring for more of. This
district has never had someone more committed to putting their body and
political career on the line to stand up to injustice, corporate
interests, or billionaire lobbies for her community.

Despite this loss, 2026 is already Justice Democrats’ most successful
cycle to date, and we still have one more primary fight tomorrow.

We’re sending at least seven new Justice Democrats to join our bloc in
Congress next year, and two more are advancing to the general election in
November — proving just how aligned our organization’s mission and
candidates are with the Democratic Party’s most reliable voters.

Thank you again for anything you contributed to support Cori and her team
in MO-01.

In solidarity,

Alexandra Rojas
Executive Director

# **Far-left El-Sayed defeats Stevens in closest major progressive primary win of the cycle**
Dr. Abdul El-Sayed narrowly **[defeated Rep. Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/redirect/7c37f534-27ab-4dad-933d-2fb8747652b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary Wednesday, winning by fewer than 15,000 votes out of more than 1.5 million cast -- a surprisingly tight margin after polls showed him leading by double digits.
[| | | | | Senate Republicans
---
@NRSC
Democrats have chosen the most radical Senate candidate in America: Abdul El-Sayed. He has shown us who he is - an extreme socialist who is dangerous and wrong for Michigan.
| 12:00 PM * Aug 5, 2026 * 37.5K Views47 Replies * 95 Reposts * 259 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/554e2452-5c3c-4c86-9ec5-e1727fbd4f47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The race became the most expensive Democratic Senate primary in history,** with over $80 million spent. El-Sayed, backed by Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, ran on Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and ending US aid to Israel.

* **The victory is the far-left 's most significant midterm win yet** because it came in a purple state -- unlike DSA victories in deep-blue New York and Colorado districts. El-Sayed would become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate if he defeats Republican Mike Rogers in November.
* **Rogers predicted El-Sayed 's bruising primary would create a "coalition problem"** heading into the general election, which Democrats view as critical to flipping Senate control.

# **DSA continues primary sweep as McKinney ousts Michigan incumbent Thanedar**
State Rep. Donavan McKinney, backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, **[defeated incumbent Rep. Shri Thanedar](https://substack.com/redirect/084f480c-aeda-47b9-b92c-81543c3c9a21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Michigan's 13th Congressional District Tuesday, extending the DSA's remarkable primary winning streak.
[| | | | | Metro Detroit News
---
@metrodetroitn
🚨: State Rep. Donavan McKinney has won the Democratic primary for Michigan's 13th Congressional District, defeating incumbent U.S. Rep. Shri Thanedar.
| 2:06 PM * Aug 5, 2026 * 270 Views2 Replies * 1 Repost * 9 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/b62ffd5b-d667-4477-bb17-fb055f803b76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The victory adds to a wave of socialist primary wins this cycle** that includes unseating veteran incumbents in New York, Colorado, and now Michigan -- with DSA-aligned candidates consistently toppling establishment Democrats.

* **Thanedar 's defeat is notable because he is himself a progressive** -- but broke with the DSA in October 2023 over his support for Israel following the Hamas attacks, making him a target for the movement's more anti-Israel faction. McKinney campaigned on affordability, climate justice, and portrayed Thanedar as a self-made multimillionaire too wealthy and out-of-touch to represent working constituents.
* **McKinney advances to the November general election** in a heavily Democratic district, virtually guaranteeing another DSA member joins Congress in January.

# **Ohio dad charged after shooting man accused of sexually assaulting his daughter**
Malik Chandler, 31, of Grove City, Ohio, was charged with felonious assault after **[shooting Diego Montoya Gonzalez, 20,](https://substack.com/redirect/96a21e4c-53d8-412a-a822-4d33a363217f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who is accused of sexually assaulting his 11-year-old daughter. Chandler lured Gonzalez to his home by posing as his daughter on TikTok, intending to detain him for police, but fired his weapon when he believed Gonzalez was reaching for a gun.

I have good news and bad news. I am going to start with the good, because I think you deserve to hear it. **July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign.** While Sabato's Crystal Ball was moving 14 races toward Democrats. While James Talarico's billionaire backers were writing $10 million checks. While the national environment was shifting against Republicans at every turn, Texas conservatives showed up in a way that I will never forget. You gave more in July than in any month since this campaign began. Not because a single mega-donor wrote a massive check. Because thousands of grassroots conservatives across this state and this country decided that Texas was worth fighting for. That is the good news. And it is genuinely great news. **Now here is the bad news.** **Fox News just released a new poll showing James Talarico leading me 51% to 48%. This is Fox News. Not a Democratic pollster. Not a liberal outlet._Fox News_. And their poll shows Talarico over 50% for the first time in this race.** Here is what the numbers show. Talarico has 98% of Democrats. He has 68% of independents. And 24% of non-MAGA Republicans are supporting him. That last number is the one that concerns me most. Nearly one in four Republicans who did not back President Trump is currently planning to vote for a Democrat who believes God is nonbinary, calls the American flag a complicated symbol, and wants a welcome mat at the southern border. **_I am not going to sugarcoat this. These numbers are serious._** But here is what I know. The margin of error on the Fox News poll is plus or minus 3 points. This race is not over. Among undecided voters, more lean toward me than toward Talarico. And the grassroots momentum we built in July proves that when conservatives show up, we can compete. The question is whether we can keep that momentum going into August... James Talarico has raised $70 million. He has the national media telling the story he wants told. **What I have is you, and the strongest grassroots month this campaign has ever seen.** Let us make August even stronger. clean_body: I have good news and bad news... I have good news and bad news... | | | | | | | Peter, I have good news and bad news. I am going to start with the good, because I think you deserve to hear it. July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign. While Sabato's Crystal Ball was moving 14 races toward Democrats. While James Talarico's billionaire backers were writing $10 million checks. While the national environment was shifting against Republicans at every turn, Texas conservatives showed up in a way that I will never forget. You gave more in July than in any month since this campaign began. Not because a single mega-donor wrote a massive check. Because thousands of grassroots conservatives across this state and this country decided that Texas was worth fighting for. That is the good news. And it is genuinely great news. Now here is the bad news. Fox News just released a new poll showing James Talarico leading me 51% to 48%. This is Fox News. Not a Democratic pollster. Not a liberal outlet.Fox News. And their poll shows Talarico over 50% for the first time in this race. Here is what the numbers show. Talarico has 98% of Democrats. He has 68% of independents. And 24% of non-MAGA Republicans are supporting him. That last number is the one that concerns me most. Nearly one in four Republicans who did not back President Trump is currently planning to vote for a Democrat who believes God is nonbinary, calls the American flag a complicated symbol, and wants a welcome mat at the southern border. I am not going to sugarcoat this. These numbers are serious. But here is what I know. The margin of error on the Fox News poll is plus or minus 3 points. This race is not over. Among undecided voters, more lean toward me than toward Talarico. And the grassroots momentum we built in July proves that when conservatives show up, we can compete. The question is whether we can keep that momentum going into August... James Talarico has raised $70 million. He has the national media telling the story he wants told. State's Sheriffs Unite Behind Trump-Endorsed Conservative as Louisiana's Choice for the U.S. Senate

| | |
---
| | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/14gdCABmFmJ?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a)
| | | | | | FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEAugust 5, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**LOUISIANA SHERIFFS' ASSOCIATION ENDORSES JULIA LETLOW FOR U.S. SENATE** _State's Sheriffs Unite Behind Trump-Endorsed Conservative as Louisiana's Choice for the U.S. Senate_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** – The Louisiana Sheriffs' Association announced its endorsement of Congresswoman Julia Letlow in Louisiana's race for the United States Senate, backing the Trump-endorsed conservative as the candidate law enforcement leaders trust to keep Louisiana families safe and stand up for those who wear the badge.
The endorsement comes after nearly five years of Letlow's consistent work in Congress to support law enforcement, strengthen border security, crack down on crime, and ensure officers have the resources they need to protect their communities.
_“It is the decision of the Louisiana Sheriffs’ Association to support Representative Letlow in her forthcoming election on November 3, 2026,”_ **said Louisiana Sheriffs’ Association Executive Director Kevin Cobb.**
_“The Louisiana Sheriffs’ Association has had the privilege of working proactively with Representative Letlow in Congress,”_**said Louisiana Sheriffs’ Association President Jayson Richardson.**_“We look forward to continuing that relationship with her as our Senator.”_****
_"I am incredibly honored to earn the support of the Louisiana Sheriffs' Association,”_**said Congresswoman Letlow.** “ _As your next United States Senator, I will always stand with law enforcement, secure our border, support our officers, and fight to ensure they have every tool they need to protect Louisiana families."_
Throughout her time in Congress, Letlow has been a reliable advocate for Louisiana law enforcement, supporting funding for local agencies, backing efforts to combat fentanyl and violent crime, and consistently standing with President Trump on policies that restore law and order. She has also worked to secure federal resources for public safety initiatives across Louisiana while opposing efforts to defund or weaken law enforcement.
The Louisiana Sheriffs' Association joins President Donald J. Trump, Governor Jeff Landry, Attorney General Liz Murrill, Majority Leader Steve Scalise, and conservative leaders from across Louisiana in supporting Julia Letlow's campaign for the United States Senate.
