subject: Over 90% of voters agree on this
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Democracy
body:
| |
---
Peter, A new survey from the Brennan Center for Justice just polled voters and found that there _is_ something that most Americans agree on: our government has a big, big corruption problem, and it’s time to fix it. The survey found that across party lines, over 90% of voters agree that government corruption is a pervasive problem. But there’s hope, because a majority of Americans surveyed also agree on the solution: _it’s time to get wealth and dark money out of politics, and create a system that works for the people._ **[But we want to know what you think. Can you take a moment to tell us what you would do to restore trust in our democracy?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38ckToVk2GgjHLeCx3x2RhhMUwiLOfx_s9u5NvX-QwmB8HFneI_J4DJc3z8yUtJzR0lIBEjwkJdl9Uqi-cLVhN5sOdxGFYZPaSoy8JbXVERw8NHxmDBi6tJaI2piIS2uknQ1Auza7GT_7uKOGYNaNLtsawOLYQaEVG4PcscLnvc2Vng8F2FwgiUtZLcpSHa2dWRNmt__G3XL1yY5ZtEj4gQkQm2uKGCSIWLHRGRiItNFOQ6wk8KtFT7pT5i1zoYNh181xYIPfvMkWVosA__pzGA/4sx/2xsx6scSSF2XQsIEakvIug/h0/h001.FUps8Tm_HLJIMM76RM6UFETJU50tQoPdMfrrjPdgRT8)****** As divided as our country feels right now, the Brennan Center survey showed that Americans are on the same page when it comes to feeling like our democracy is riddled with corruption. Here are some of the report’s key findings:
* More than 9 in 10 voters think corruption is a widespread systemic problem affecting all of our public institutions.
* Most defined corruption broadly. Politicians using their position for personal gain counts, and so does catering to the interests of billionaires and corporations.
* Voters agreed on why corruption happens, pointing to personal financial gain, campaign donations from billionaires and corporations, and a lack of consequences for corrupt activity as the top causes.
* From dysfunctional public services to rising prices, voters agree that government corruption impacts our daily lives.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Thank you for your support
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
This victory is proof of what’s possible when we organize together.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260805-6559-footer&t=1&akid=6559%2E420207%2E02kJFJ)
Thank you, thank you, thank you, Peter!
**Thanks to this incredible grassroots movement, we won our primary election last night.**
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260805-1.0FF4aQ&refcode=em20260805-6559&t=2&akid=6559%2E420207%2E02kJFJ)
And not only that, but we helped several other progressive candidates win across Seattle, King County, and Washington State!
**A big congratulations to Liz Berry, Jaelynn Scott, Gerry Pollet, Darya Farivar, Colleen Melody, Ian Birk, Teresa Mosqueda, and Jorge Barón** — I look forward to working with each of you to move our progressive movement forward and make life better for poor and working people in our communities. We also PASSED Proposition 1 to fund future investments in Seattle’s libraries!
But we didn’t just win here in Washington. Last night was a big night for progressives across the country. I’m proud to have endorsed **Abdul El-Sayed** and **William Lawrence** , who won their primary elections for Senate and House in Michigan, and **Tom Perriello** , who won his House primary in Virginia. I’m also so proud that my Medicare For All PAC, which is entirely funded by small dollar donors, was a top 5 contributor to Abdul’s campaign!
It’s clear that the people are tired of corporations and big money groups like AIPAC calling the shots — and it’s time for us to build a government for the _people_ , not the billionaires.
Whether you donated, volunteered, voted, shared our message, or simply stood with us, these victories were only possible because of supporters like you. From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by _people_ , not corporate PACs, not lobbyists, and not wealthy special interests.
These wins are a reminder that when we organize, when we show up, and when we fight together, we can overcome powerful opposition and keep moving our progressive movement forward.
**But our work doesn’t end here.**
The challenges facing our communities are bigger than any one election. We’re _still_ fighting to protect health care, defend our democracy, lower costs for working families, and build a future where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
[**If you’re able, will you make a contribution of $3 today to help us continue building this movement and prepare for the general election this November?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260805-1.0FF4aQ&refcode=em20260805-6559&amount=3&t=3&akid=6559%2E420207%2E02kJFJ)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260805-1.0FF4aQ&amount=3&refcode=em20260805-6559&t=22&akid=6559%2E420207%2E02kJFJ)**
Thank you again for believing in this campaign and for standing with me. This primary victory gives us the momentum we need for the fight ahead, and I’m so grateful to have you by my side. I can’t wait to see what more we’ll accomplish together.
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

A Maryland school district in Anne Arundel County is transitioning kids while keeping it a secret. The mother of one of the children said, in her own words, that the school "was secretly helping their daughter pretend to be male at school."
Donald Trump and his administration are now getting involved and fighting back.
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon wrote a scathing demand to the school district:
"By categorically withholding 'information about a student's gender identity' from parents except where 'legally required,' AACPS appears to have adopted a blanket, district-wide practice of nondisclosure untethered to FERPA's enumerated exceptions ... parents were denied access to their child's full record, information was disclosed without parental consent, and the parents were denied a hearing to correct the record. Comply with the law or face us in Court."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/84db0092-8902-4a1d-9306-4f1d76f71c93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Essentially, the school district implemented a policy of restricting parents from seeing their own children's health records.
Think about this for a second.
The school district had more of a right to information on children than their own parents.
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon cited The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) for her legal challenge against this insane policy. FERPA says that parents have the legal right to access their children's educational records, and Trump argues that this includes anything related to gender and sex.

# **Exec Order 14155 creates new health benefit for seniors**
## _**Now it 's time to claim it**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6772d65c-dc32-4564-b5ad-07b5e2fdacfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**ATTENTION:**
Are you an American taxpayer?
Are you over the age of 54?
Thanks to President Trump's Executive Order 14155, you are entitled to a new health benefit.
**[Click here to claim it now.](https://substack.com/redirect/6772d65c-dc32-4564-b5ad-07b5e2fdacfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Learn More](https://substack.com/redirect/6772d65c-dc32-4564-b5ad-07b5e2fdacfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
_**(Piece continues)**_
Fox News **[reported](https://substack.com/redirect/13ffecea-8ccb-4f5f-9175-1a4cc1cc2221?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that this law has "been used by the DOJ in attempts to overturn similar policies in Maine and California."
"School districts that hide information from parents are violating federal law," Dhillon said. "FERPA is not optional, and any districts that attempt to bypass or distort its requirements should expect immediate federal action. In partnership with the Department of Education, the Department of Justice will initiate enforcement proceedings with districts that fail to comply."
This is another reason why federalism is so important and the Department of Education is an evil agency. Red states can prosecute and punish school districts for doing this on the state level, even when Democrats are in the White House. On the flip side, the Department of Education can try to bypass those states, even if they are doing the right thing.
Stories like these are a good reminder that the uniparty is not a thing. What's the uniparty? The idea that no matter who gets elected, Republican or Democrat, the outcome in American politics is basically the same. This is incredibly short-sighted.
Do we really think a Kamala Harris administration would challenge this Maryland school district? They would probably give them more funding. Do we really think that male student-athletes would be banned from women's sports? Of course not; a Kamala Harris presidency would have seen unprecedented levels of trans athletes ruining women's collegiate sports.
The bottom line is that elections have real, tangible consequences for our children and our families. The Trump administration taking a hardline stance against these rogue school districts proves that who sits in the Oval Office actually matters. It's time to finally put the uniparty myth to rest, and keep fighting to put parents back in charge of their children's education and health.

I have some big news:

**SEIU California -- which represents more than 750,000 workers across this state -- just endorsed our campaign. And I'm the only candidate in this race with their support.**

[](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquO38L98SklfBdoDq94y0bmNpGkqxcvbwAwPTl2twJS_GKRmZzDVTtx3yAPcb-ZhUx8Ws7nUgQPjZekxmsBE7tq2ihmSjwPC0MK_aeYtlG4V5rNq_deDqA3lanTcmUIPME0wvG5-3d0QAzTJT2dsFKP83iVeuO_tPL6KI8RKsZ3XQ_gyd66z61RHqRqS3iigxPTyAZxhgcG7x4XOLr0ju0uS-uQKdqsgQ9vMnwyLe3DDQTZ75lOqhLuCn98P1rROyJjqoV5NqF2aSlX60N-59Q1ljGUpOoOJ3e6Fbwq4Q4gxf9iOv0WjZpKK-2_QlSf8tIXuxoF1eSvd7N-RpmBlAey4B7MaZDBIKJG-ReBCA6VEfbEc4hiUi4iVURypT6fezU/4sx/4e57kQKZRzao7F85gXIYIA/h1/h001.BGeJ-TguBSz9T2TNlc-EBhqv9lij4p5ssLzCQhcOUmU)
One of the largest and most powerful labor unions in California looked at this race, looked at a 21-year incumbent, and chose us.

Historically, endorsements like these almost always go to the incumbent, no questions asked. But working people are done with the status quo. They're frustrated with a political establishment that has failed to protect them -- and they're hungry for a new generation of leadership that will actually fight for them.

As a proud member of the California Faculty Association, I know that the labor movement is leading the fight to reclaim our democracy and our economy for working people in this country, and I am so proud to have their support in this race.

body:
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1317?t=1&akid=999%2E3892029%2EeD85RZ)

| | | | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
| Hi, Alex Vindman here.Alex Vindman
And I’m his twin brother, Eugene.Eugene Vindman |
| Younger brother...Alex Vindman
By nine minutes, Alex...Eugene Vindman |
| Our family left everything behind to flee from tyranny. We came to America on Christmas Day, with just a few suitcases and hope for a better future.Alex Vindman
Our dad worked long hours as a furniture mover. He taught himself English at night, learning ten new English words every day.Eugene Vindman |
| The first years were tough, but he made sure to instill in us a love for our country.Alex Vindman
Something we both have always carried with us — through reporting the phone call that led to Trump's first impeachment to my winning campaign for Congress to serve the people of Virginia.Eugene Vindman |
| Now I'm running for Senate in Florida — one of the most flippable Senate seats in the country.Alex Vindman
But Alex can't do this alone. He needs us with him — like he was there for all of us when he had the courage to stand up to Trump.Eugene Vindman |
| It's true, I need your help. Alex Vindman
That's why we're here together, asking:Eugene Vindman |
| [****Can you please use this link to make a $3 contribution to my campaign for U.S. Senate? Do it before our campaign has to make some of the most important budget decisions of the race.****](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/avvf-digi-em-q32026?refcode=em260805-2&amount=3&refcode2=999_3892029_eD85RZ&akid=999%2E3892029%2EeD85RZ) Alex Vindman
If everyone reading this chipped in even just a few bucks, Alex would have the resources we need to win his race and flip the Senate.Eugene Vindman |
| But not everyone does.Alex Vindman
So we're counting on those who understand how important this race is to help out today.Eugene Vindman |

# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=621%2E127862%2EQJBOvH)
Donald Trump is in Nevada _today,_ and there’s no doubt in my mind that our opponent, Joe Lombardo, welcomed him to our state with open arms.
**Lombardo doesn’t stand up to Trump because he actively carries out the MAGA agenda here in Nevada.**
→ Lombardo backs Trump’s tariffs that raise costs on working people and doesn’t care about how it affects families.
→ He cheered on Trump’s reckless war with Iran.
→ He supports Trump’s efforts to end mail-in voting.
→ **Lombardo is Trump’s #1 cheerleader every step of the way.**
Trump and his MAGA allies have their eyes on our campaign — which means this race is going to be close and expensive.
Here's why: **Trump knows Nevada is one of the most competitive governor's races in the country, a race Republicans need to win.**

El-Sayed Topples Michigan Dem Establishment
Abdul El-Sayed narrowly defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan's [Democratic Senate primary](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LHOpCAUxfGnwQ6DCMIWFNvYzbZbmrtw1ZugGC4zE99-4yt8zSnPL_n_fS0voEzn9gcODMS8pJIWLpEgEzf-0glnaTvWhMdVF630JJWXyi4QG31wMdClYPXgV99hGJy3v5wZten2EL0CjHGdXErKDSt6M0Q3KGPQxWGyHYXnT3ll9Wi9GXvrwabktXfWqtVNwqj3laBhTydTQo6lXFfJ1ChyX-rW5bC3drEYfws9Cz0noHxHyBlrH8sh9PwQQs_KP2OFnuFfemeJWTLcmOQOGW_JDT94sjwo7rTBKRlPaCivSgfUW-i5qyFdX8qZeHLCqO0Ayo_RtZ-G-wT9PwAA__8M_n7U), a stinging blow to a party establishment that poured tens of millions into Stevens. The former public-health official rode endorsements from Bernie Sanders and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to a 48.5%–47.5% [upset victory](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckDmO3TAQBU9DZRI4lLgoYOBE2Th1KDTIHqkBbmBzvuzbG99HcPaiV6j69Xl-AiUq10_I6In5jDWeXANBIh78UIFSx409Ym79VFKZWbpZ6hPCoBeeG0zRa_XhvtyE_sM6vdttVdt0-82EAEZKHa2RFmC3YAMEs0eLuFuYyL__pJNardpt66Id6BidclZr-WWN2OR3izBwocIUkUOtrdVEgwIvtV9T8vcYjcX6Q6hDqON5nuUBvqlcoxb8DZkK9iXULNRR8GGhjgC5AV3l367l6shMtUAS6tiMXbWSQh2Zwk0XlJmxwMA5Yq6hw6Awt04Z-p-5I3-nwfPbQqhj6j62h1IiNlZs8spA6Y2exv-mfXn1NwAA__9tmIyh). His win extends a national socialist surge and lays bare Democratic fractures over Israel, ICE, and Medicare for All heading into November. El-Sayed now faces Republican Mike Rogers in one of the cycle's most competitive [Senate contests](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLFurDAQRb8GOiNjYzCFi9fQ7WtTIq9ngFGMjRjvkv37aCPlB9Jf3XN0Pm7zzVOktP73OzpiniHDzDmQj8SFL0o-5bLhCbgf56yk6oW0QprZh0JPnDtfgzOqtYut0bWDNePQadXVmwvaQgvK3rUM_QjajrJVRi9GgdWjNTW595-00ihtbKcbY70BsMoOxshl6KtOPg7wBRtKTIAccj6OHKlQ4Cafax3dVsrBlf5XqalS03VdzZK_El7chLxXavqdV2r6sd8JCp47Cy6-oMiLOKJ_iU98idMHZPFIS44guOATEwuMgv0LQdx9KRHFTmGj1af6dHBcFCNxP1SdXHdP8c2sy19DPp36DgAA___WRIZ5), a race that could decide control of the chamber. Conservatives see a gift: a self-described democratic socialist atop a battleground ticket in a must-win swing state. ★★★
A Good Night for Trump Endorsements
President Trump's grip on the Republican field held firm on the biggest primary night of the cycle. In Kansas, Trump-backed state Senate President Ty Masterson won a crowded [gubernatorial field](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2S3CAUBODToEwqBoFgAwInytapQ9VbYKRXy1_x2MFze9fMEZx19FV3__k8PgEj5vM3pGCR6PDFH1QcQkTqNDBDLv0KzYdU2yG42GZuZq4OcB0f4ZAweavEzdzNFOxNG_Wh5SrkdNk1qA9juBBfWstNqS-Qd-cMaC5XtXI-oX153HAlVmXkuigDynsjjFaK3_XGJP-pHnpYMBP6QK6UWkvEjo6W0s4p2qv3Smz9xcTOxD7GWAbQhfnsJYe_kDCHtriSmNhzGMTE7iBVwDO_c8lnC0RYMkQmdrlpJW-Kif09tTZM0J5ziMF1LJnmDt8BBjxpTuguPCHPCYnKT8P5GzLBS52a9XVgjEibZpKfCTC-Skz9f09-WPEvAAD__6QNj4g) with 43%, an outcome that had looked unsettled before the president's intervention. In Missouri, Trump-endorsed state Sen. Rick Brattin captured a [redrawn district](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLGunTAQRL8GOiOz2OBXuEhDd9OmRHttA6sYG3l9Ifn7iHzCK0cjzRydX6_lhRQpbT_xCJaYF5_9wtkRRuLKNyVMue6h-HCcZQEJo5BGSL2gq3SFRWHrrYberKYNtp-M_prUAKrdLY76_ZZglFx7wLWHIbgA71F9jWM_rX1L9tmTRmoYtFFDpw1q7w2YSWu5TmOj5Of0WENHickHdjmfZ45UyXGXy9ZGu9d6cjP8aGBuYL7vu1vznxRu7lw-GpgjXUE8uYH5P_5Z6MDyV4QYXKWcRAn8iZXFQW6nDZO4qGyUCMVvTIxPwZw_hcSNvFPaak5tsf68KUbicWqU3A6k-Dy29bsaLwv_AgAA__-n1ocT) engineered to flip a long-held Democratic seat, validating the president's push for GOP-friendly maps. The results underscore Trump's continued dominance over primary voters even as Democrats' left wing ascends. Republicans enter the fall defending a narrow House majority with the president's coalition intact, energized, and increasingly confident that redistricting foresight will pay dividends in November. ★★★
Lebanon Peace Talks Falter
U.S.-brokered talks between Israel and Lebanon hit turbulence in Rome this week, ending Tuesday's session early "due to events on the ground" before Israeli airstrikes resumed against [Hezbollah positions](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2OpDAUBODTQGZk_AMmcLAJWW-6IXqNH82TjG3Z7vZqTj9Cc4MJK_lUVf8e2wPIU3j9hQstlbK56LYSdwJPpZZGAUKsJ2aHV8qb4GJi3DCuN9grfXBT0DurxWgO06MdZ6OXWUmh-tOq-ZC4wJPL8UCpxkkuwPUuuFr0E4Xuyd4eN1wLqY2SgzagnTPCzFrzY546xd_JQcWBQiGHZY8xpeip0l6GmF-9t2etqXTyTyfWTqytteGI_wO2Muzx6sTq6YPszp1YKUNgDTKr-X0l5hA8KzUDVRYPdsZ8vb9Yxpgw_Kxkd8E-W5caeU9lmjvFXxeQv_W-_vayjxXfAQAA__9sLX0s) across the south. Negotiators pressed forward Wednesday on the Trilateral Framework, which trades an eventual Israeli withdrawal for the disarmament of the Iran-backed [terror group](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LHOniAUxvGrwQ2DCIIDQxe3r2tHc4SjnnwIBuhr06tvvIXuT35P8v_1tX4BRUrHT7jQUa1ryGGt2RNEqq0-lCDldmIJeN1llUJOXFgu9Aq-0QdXBV1wWg52tx26wVg9GzVK1Z1uMvM0230btBm3edAqhFHuQmkR_Ky87ci9nrBCy1FbNfbagg7BSmu0FruZmBK_7wANe0qVAlaf833nSI187XM5uujO1u7Kxh9MLkwuz_P0D9ST0tFywj9wUcLS-3wxuSR86rvJJQYmFzWZScyGyYVqAYy8tkLfWPmJf7ccI5w84gYpJ17yhfxG8MgbxO9X6YoL90MxUp0MU-K4gOJ71LX_Dflx8l8AAAD__59mhYg). Lebanon demands a full pullout ahead of any disarmament, while Israel insists Hezbollah lay down its arms first and points to the group's continued rocket capability. The Trump administration, which brokered June's framework, called the technical progress "extremely productive" despite the friction, and negotiators are set to reconvene Thursday morning. A durable agreement would mark another regional win for the president's pressure-first diplomacy following this year's campaign against Iran.
El-Sayed Faces Rogers Next

Michigan's Senate battleground is set: socialist nominee Abdul El-Sayed against Republican Mike Rogers, who [cleared the field](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LHOpCAUxfGnwQ6DCMIWFNvYzbZbmrtw1ZugGC4zE99-4yt8zSnPL_n_fS0voEzn9gcODMS8pJIWLpEgEzf-0glnaTvWhMdVF630JJWXyi4QG31wMdClYPXgV99hGJy3v5wZten2EL0CjHGdXErKDSt6M0Q3KGPQxWGyHYXnT3ll9Wi9GXvrwabktXfWqtVNwqj3laBhTydTQo6lXFfJ1ChyX-rW5bC3drEYfws9Cz0noHxHyBlrH8sh9PwQQs_KP2OFnuFfemeJWTLcmOQOGW_JDT94sjwo7rTBKRlPaCivSgfUW-i5qyFdX8qZeHLCqO0Ayo_RtZ-G-wT9PwAA__8M_n7U) Tuesday. El-Sayed enters the general as the underdog in a state Republicans badly want to flip.

In Missouri's St. Louis-based 1st District, Rep. Wesley Bell again defeated former "Squad" member Cori Bush in a [primary rematch](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2S3CAUBODToEwqBoFgAwInytapQ9VbYKRXy1_x2MFze9fMEZx19FV3__k8PgEj5vM3pGCR6PDFH1QcQkTqNDBDLv0KzYdU2yG42GZuZq4OcB0f4ZAweavEzdzNFOxNG_Wh5SrkdNk1qA9juBBfWstNqS-Qd-cMaC5XtXI-oX153HAlVmXkuigDynsjjFaK3_XGJP-pHnpYMBP6QK6UWkvEjo6W0s4p2qv3Smz9xcTOxD7GWAbQhfnsJYe_kDCHtriSmNhzGMTE7iBVwDO_c8lnC0RYMkQmdrlpJW-Kif09tTZM0J5ziMF1LJnmDt8BBjxpTuguPCHPCYnKT8P5GzLBS52a9XVgjEibZpKfCTC-Skz9f09-WPEvAAD__6QNj4g), a rare establishment win on a night otherwise dominated by the insurgent left.

★★★
Tlaib Cruises To Renomination

Progressive Rep. Rashida Tlaib easily won her Michigan [Democratic primary](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLGunTAQRL8GOiOz2OBXuEhDd9OmRHttA6sYG3l9Ifn7iHzCK0cjzRydX6_lhRQpbT_xCJaYF5_9wtkRRuLKNyVMue6h-HCcZQEJo5BGSL2gq3SFRWHrrYberKYNtp-M_prUAKrdLY76_ZZglFx7wLWHIbgA71F9jWM_rX1L9tmTRmoYtFFDpw1q7w2YSWu5TmOj5Of0WENHickHdjmfZ45UyXGXy9ZGu9d6cjP8aGBuYL7vu1vznxRu7lw-GpgjXUE8uYH5P_5Z6MDyV4QYXKWcRAn8iZXFQW6nDZO4qGyUCMVvTIxPwZw_hcSNvFPaak5tsf68KUbicWqU3A6k-Dy29bsaLwv_AgAA__-n1ocT) and is on track for a fifth term, reinforcing the party's leftward drift in safe blue seats this cycle.

* * *

With courts unwinding his emergency duties, the administration is leaning on Section 338 of the 1930 Smoot-Hawley Act as its [tariff fallback](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D1yhCAUAODTYKeDT1AsKNLYbdqUzlt-9M0gMMCuOX5mr5ALfMX389gfSIHi8Y2X01TrbpPdazKEgWqrN0WMqZ2uWHflsgOHueeq53JH0-jtdoGd1RJG5VXn9LgouS5iAtGdGtWqrESlpJnMvE7zyNdlhdE_5fr0jnekPx5XXMIklZgGqVBaq0AtUnK_zEzwV7bY3ECxknXVpJRzCtTI1CGVowv6bC1XNn0x2Bhs930PN9aT4tFSdL94UXRlMOlisFHcfTKvymAT8yImKRhsrbyu3Dcs5H2fA8b-2Z9YeyyF3s4y2Lqibb4pBKrzwgQ_LqTwIbv237K3hr8AAAD__3zUfVs), keeping trade leverage alive while the Supreme Court weighs the broader case. ★★★

Attention shifts to the judiciary as the Supreme Court prepares to open next term with a [major climate case](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LHOniAUxvGrwQ2DCIIDQxe3r2tHc4SjnnwIBuhr06tvvIXuT35P8v_1tX4BRUrHT7jQUa1ryGGt2RNEqq0-lCDldmIJeN1llUJOXFgu9Aq-0QdXBV1wWg52tx26wVg9GzVK1Z1uMvM0230btBm3edAqhFHuQmkR_Ky87ci9nrBCy1FbNfbagg7BSmu0FruZmBK_7wANe0qVAlaf833nSI187XM5uujO1u7Kxh9MLkwuz_P0D9ST0tFywj9wUcLS-3wxuSR86rvJJQYmFzWZScyGyYVqAYy8tkLfWPmJf7ccI5w84gYpJ17yhfxG8MgbxO9X6YoL90MxUp0MU-K4gOJ71LX_Dflx8l8AAAD__59mhYg) and November arguments pending on climate change regulations and illegal alien detention policies.

★★★
Congress Stays In Recess

The House and Senate remain out through August, leaving no floor votes scheduled. The action has moved to executive orders and the courts, with the SAVE Act, appropriations, and a looming government-funding deadline all waiting for members to return after Labor Day.

* * *
1. **Talarico Leads Paxton** — a Texas Southern University poll became the [latest survey](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLGOwyAQRL8Gd7YIBntTUFzjLtdeaW1g7ayEAQEX5_NP_oUrRxo9zbyfx_pADhz3bzzIcq2rT36tyTEGrq2eHDGm9qLi6chlVVJNvYRemhVd4zetGjtvjbrBBh3Z2wzmPutR6e5ljUYnJTiaAbaJ9PO5mbsbUTpPAHTv2F48CdKo0YAeBwNovAcFszFymyeh5W_22GjgWNlTdSnlnAI3dnVIZe-CfbWWqxi_hFqEWs7zHAphcIGw5BSub4NLh1DLlapQS6WIjYRadopUMAi1XDOEWhp98Go0DFjYpf5d-4yflmJXrM8nh8B1moWW-4EcLm7X_mvtbdVfAAAA___5Ln-T) showing Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton.

* * *
1. **The Left's New Face
** El-Sayed's win hands Republicans a [potent contrast](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LHOpCAUxfGnwQ6DCMIWFNvYzbZbmrtw1ZugGC4zE99-4yt8zSnPL_n_fS0voEzn9gcODMS8pJIWLpEgEzf-0glnaTvWhMdVF630JJWXyi4QG31wMdClYPXgV99hGJy3v5wZten2EL0CjHGdXErKDSt6M0Q3KGPQxWGyHYXnT3ll9Wi9GXvrwabktXfWqtVNwqj3laBhTydTQo6lXFfJ1ChyX-rW5bC3drEYfws9Cz0noHxHyBlrH8sh9PwQQs_KP2OFnuFfemeJWTLcmOQOGW_JDT94sjwo7rTBKRlPaCivSgfUW-i5qyFdX8qZeHLCqO0Ayo_RtZ-G-wT9PwAA__8M_n7U) — a democratic socialist atop a swing-state ticket is a general-election gift.

** Trump's primary-night [batting average](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2S3CAUBODToEwqBoFgAwInytapQ9VbYKRXy1_x2MFze9fMEZx19FV3__k8PgEj5vM3pGCR6PDFH1QcQkTqNDBDLv0KzYdU2yG42GZuZq4OcB0f4ZAweavEzdzNFOxNG_Wh5SrkdNk1qA9juBBfWstNqS-Qd-cMaC5XtXI-oX153HAlVmXkuigDynsjjFaK3_XGJP-pHnpYMBP6QK6UWkvEjo6W0s4p2qv3Smz9xcTOxD7GWAbQhfnsJYe_kDCHtriSmNhzGMTE7iBVwDO_c8lnC0RYMkQmdrlpJW-Kif09tTZM0J5ziMF1LJnmDt8BBjxpTuguPCHPCYnKT8P5GzLBS52a9XVgjEibZpKfCTC-Skz9f09-WPEvAAD__6QNj4g) proves his sway over GOP voters remains the most valuable currency in Republican politics.

** The party's [redistricting foresight](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLGunTAQRL8GOiOz2OBXuEhDd9OmRHttA6sYG3l9Ifn7iHzCK0cjzRydX6_lhRQpbT_xCJaYF5_9wtkRRuLKNyVMue6h-HCcZQEJo5BGSL2gq3SFRWHrrYberKYNtp-M_prUAKrdLY76_ZZglFx7wLWHIbgA71F9jWM_rX1L9tmTRmoYtFFDpw1q7w2YSWu5TmOj5Of0WENHickHdjmfZ45UyXGXy9ZGu9d6cjP8aGBuYL7vu1vznxRu7lw-GpgjXUE8uYH5P_5Z6MDyV4QYXKWcRAn8iZXFQW6nDZO4qGyUCMVvTIxPwZw_hcSNvFPaak5tsf68KUbicWqU3A6k-Dy29bsaLwv_AgAA__-n1ocT) in Missouri may matter more in November than any single primary upset this week.
